working_title: Earth, Oppressed by Demon-Kings, Seeks Brahma
one_line_summary: The Earth, burdened by arrogant demon kings, takes the form of a weeping cow and appeals to Brahma for relief.

working_title: Vishnu Promises to Descend into the House of Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Brahma and the gods carry the Earth's plea to Vishnu on the milk ocean; a divine voice declares Vishnu will be born in Vasudeva's house and that the gods should descend as helpers.

working_title: The Doom Prophecy Warns Kamsa of Devaki's Eighth Child
one_line_summary: At Vasudeva's wedding procession, Kamsa drives the chariot and hears a bodiless voice declare that Devaki's eighth child will slay him.
variant_notes: BP/VP: a bodiless heavenly voice warns at the wedding; HV: Narada delivers the warning. VP 5.1 also folds in the pacification beat.

working_title: Vasudeva Pacifies Kamsa and Promises to Surrender His Sons
one_line_summary: Kamsa seizes Devaki to kill her, but Vasudeva placates him with reasoning and vows to surrender every newborn son to him.
variant_notes: See also 'prophecy' (VP 5.1 combines warning + pacification).

working_title: Kamsa Imprisons Devaki and Destroys Her Children
one_line_summary: After Narada reveals that the gods are incarnating among the Yadavas, Kamsa imprisons Devaki and Vasudeva and kills each child as it is born.

working_title: Kamsa's Ministers Counsel Slaughtering the Righteous
one_line_summary: Kamsa's demon ministers urge him to kill all newborn children and to destroy the brahmanas, cows and all in whom Vishnu dwells.

working_title: Kamsa Orders the Slaughter of Children and the Pious
one_line_summary: Kamsa dispatches shape-shifting demons across the land to massacre the sages' and infants' protectors, and returns to his palace.
variant_notes: VP 5.4 also includes the release of Vasudeva and Devaki.

working_title: Vishnu Resolves to Incarnate to Relieve the Earth
one_line_summary: Narada tells Vishnu that the gods' incarnations alone cannot destroy the demons reborn as kings, and urges him to descend himself.
variant_notes: VP: Earth petitions at Meru and Vishnu plucks black/white hairs; HV: Narada urges Vishnu, Brahma foretells the birth.

working_title: Devaki's Seventh Embryo Is Transferred to Rohini (Balarama Born)
one_line_summary: The seventh embryo is transferred from Devaki to Rohini by the goddess of sleep, and the child is born as Sankarshana (Balarama).
characters: Devaki; Rohini; goddess of sleep; Balarama
variant_notes: Execution of the command in 'command_yogamaya'; see also 'conception' (VP 5.2 covers this transfer).

working_title: Kamsa Repents and Devaki Forgives Him
one_line_summary: Kansa, ashamed, confesses to Devaki and throws himself at her feet; Devaki forgives him, saying Time alone is the instrument.
variant_notes: HV-specific; BP 10.4.2 folds repentance into the Yogamaya episode.

working_title: The Conception of Devaki and the Six Demon Embryos
one_line_summary: Vishnu enters Vasudeva's mind; Devaki conceives the Lord and glows with brilliance, and Kamsa, though uneasy, refrains from harming her.
variant_notes: HV gives the backstory (six Saragarbha demons cursed by Hiranyakashipu); BP omits the six-embryo detail.

working_title: The Gods Praise the Unborn Lord in Devaki's Womb
one_line_summary: Brahma, Shiva and the host of gods descend to praise the unborn Lord in Devaki's womb and then depart.

working_title: Krishna Is Born at Midnight in the Prison
one_line_summary: At a supremely auspicious hour, with nature rejoicing, Krishna is born of Devaki in the prison at midnight.
variant_notes: VP 5.3 also includes the four-armed form and withholding of it (see 'reveal_form').

working_title: Krishna Reveals His Divine Form and Recalls Past Births
one_line_summary: The infant reveals a four-armed form bearing conch and discus; Vasudeva and Devaki praise him, and he recalls his earlier births to them before resuming an ordinary infant form.
variant_notes: See also 'birth' (VP 5.3 folds this in).

working_title: Kamsa Comes to Slay the Newborn Girl
one_line_summary: Awakened by the guards, Kamsa rushes to the prison and snatches the newborn girl from Devaki, who pleads for her life.
variant_notes: See also 'yogamaya_warn' (the dashing that follows).

working_title: Uddhava Recalls Krishna's Birth and Removal to Vraja
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls that Krishna was born of Vasudeva and Devaki in Bhoja's prison to relieve the earth's burden, and was carried by his father, fearing Kamsa, to Nanda's Vraja, where he lived hidden for eleven years with Balarama.
characters: Krishna; Vasudeva; Devaki; Nanda; Balarama; Kamsa
themes: birth; removal to Gokula; protection; divine descent
variant_notes: Compressed recollection spanning the birth and exchange (see 'birth','exchange').

working_title: Nanda Brings the Infants Home to Gokula
one_line_summary: Set at liberty, Vasudeva bids Nanda take both Krishna and Balarama to Gokula to be reared as his own sons; Nanda and the cowherds return with their waggons.

working_title: Vasudeva Carries Krishna Out of Prison Across the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Prompted by the Lord, Vasudeva carries the baby out; the prison doors open by themselves, Shesha shelters them from rain, and the Yamuna parts to give passage.
variant_notes: VP 5.3 also includes the exchange at Gokula (see 'exchange').

working_title: Vasudeva Exchanges Krishna for Yashoda's Daughter
one_line_summary: Vasudeva places Krishna in Yasoda's bed in Nanda's Gokula and carries Yasoda's newborn daughter back to Mathura.

working_title: Nanda Celebrates the Birth of His Son
one_line_summary: Nanda performs the birth rites with lavish gifts of cows and gold, and the whole of Gokula rejoices over the newborn child.

working_title: Nanda Visits Mathura and Meets Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Nanda goes to Mathura to pay his annual tribute, and Vasudeva joyfully embraces him as a brother.

working_title: Vasudeva Warns Nanda of Danger in Gokula
one_line_summary: Vasudeva affectionately inquires after his sons and urges Nanda to return quickly to Gokula, for evil omens are gathering there.

working_title: Putana Enters Gokula Disguised as a Woman
one_line_summary: Kamsa's agent Putana, a demoness who kills infants, disguises herself as a beautiful woman and enters Nanda's village.
variant_notes: See also 'putana_kill'.

working_title: Krishna Drains the Demoness Putana's Life
one_line_summary: Putana offers the baby her poisoned breast, but Krishna sucks out her very life-breath, and she falls dead, revealing her true demon form.
variant_notes: bpc1_032 is Uddhava's recollection of the same episode.

working_title: The Villagers Burn Putana's Body
one_line_summary: The gopis perform protective rites over the child, and the cowherds cut up and burn Putana's vast corpse, from which rises a fragrant smoke, for she attained a mother's reward.

working_title: The Infant Krishna Overturns the Cart with His Foot
one_line_summary: During the birth ceremonies, the unattended infant kicks the great cart, shattering it and scattering its vessels, to the astonishment of all.

working_title: Trinavarta the Whirlwind Carries Off the Baby
one_line_summary: Kamsa's servant Trinavarta, in the form of a whirlwind, snatches the child away, blinding Gokula with dust as Yasoda searches in vain.

working_title: Trinavarta Is Crushed by the Child's Weight
one_line_summary: Unable to carry the ever-heavier baby through the sky, Trinavarta falls onto a rock and is crushed, while the child is found safe on his chest.

working_title: Yasoda Sees the Universe in the Nursing Child's Mouth
one_line_summary: As Yasoda nurses the yawning child, she glimpses the whole cosmos within his open mouth and trembles in wonder.

working_title: Garga Secretly Names Rama and Krishna
one_line_summary: The family priest Garga, sent by Vasudeva, secretly performs the naming ceremony, calling the boys Rama and Krishna, and foretells their glories.

working_title: Krishna and Rama's Childhood Pranks and Butter-Stealing
one_line_summary: The two boys crawl and toddle about Gokula, and Krishna steals butter and curds from the gopis' homes with playful tricks.

working_title: Krishna Eats Mud and Shows the Cosmos in His Mouth
one_line_summary: Accused of eating dirt, Krishna opens his mouth before Yasoda, who sees the entire universe within it and is overwhelmed.

working_title: Krishna Breaks the Butter Pot
one_line_summary: While Yasoda churns, the hungry child climbs onto her lap; when she leaves, he breaks the churn-pot, steals the butter and feeds it to the monkeys, then flees as she chases him.

working_title: Yasoda Binds Krishna to the Mortar
one_line_summary: Yasoda tries to tie the mischievous Krishna with a rope, but every rope falls short by two fingers, until, moved by her effort, he lets himself be bound.
variant_notes: HV 1.62 and VP 5.6 fold this binding into the uprooting episode (see 'uproot_trees').

working_title: Krishna Uproots the Twin Arjuna Trees (Named Damodara)
one_line_summary: Dragging the mortar to which he is tied, the crawling Krishna passes between the two trees and uproots them.
variant_notes: HV/VP fold in the mortar-binding beat.

working_title: The Two Devotees Are Liberated from the Trees
one_line_summary: From the fallen trees emerge two radiant beings who bow to Krishna, praise him, and, released from their curse, depart to the north.

working_title: The Fruit-Seller Receives a Gift of Jewels
one_line_summary: Krishna takes grain to barter for fruit, but the fruit-seller's basket fills with gems as her fruit spills into his hands.

working_title: The Cowherds Decide to Migrate to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Citing the many evil omens that have befallen Gokula, the elder Upananda persuades the cowherds to migrate with their herds.
variant_notes: BP: prompted by Upananda citing omens; VP: alarmed by Putana's death, the waggon and the trees.

working_title: Krishna Conjures Wolves to Move the Milkmen to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Desiring a new forest, Krishna produces hundreds of wolves from his body to terrify the milkmen so they will abandon Vraja for Vrindavan.
variant_notes: HV's version of the migration; BP/VP attribute the move to omens/portents instead (see 'migrate_decision').

working_title: Uddhava Recalls Krishna's Cowherd Childhood and Kamsa's Demons
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls Krishna's childhood in Vraja — herding calves and cows with the cowherd boys on the Yamuna, playing the flute — and how he playfully defeated the shape-shifting demons Kamsa sent against him.
characters: Krishna; Balarama; the cowherd boys; Kamsa's demons
variant_notes: General recollection; see specific demon episodes.

working_title: Krishna Notices the Twin Arjuna Trees
one_line_summary: While his mother is busy, Krishna sees the two arjuna trees that were once the guhyaka sons of Kubera, Nalakuvara and Manigriva.

working_title: Narada Curses Nalakuvara and Manigriva
one_line_summary: Drunk and naked in a river with celestial women, Kubera's sons insult Narada, who curses them to become twin arjuna trees until Krishna's touch frees them.

working_title: The Cowherds Settle in Vrindavan
one_line_summary: The cowherd community journeys with their herds and carts and settles in Vrindavan, forming their camp in a crescent of wagons.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Calf-Demon Vatsasura
one_line_summary: The boys take up calf-herding, and Krishna seizes the demon Vatsasura, who has taken the form of a calf, and hurls him dead into a kapittha tree.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Crane-Demon Bakasura
one_line_summary: The crane-demon Bakasura, Kamsa's ally, swallows Krishna, but Krishna burns and tears him apart and frees himself.

working_title: Aghasura Becomes a Giant Python
one_line_summary: Aghasura, brother of Putana and Bakasura, takes the form of a vast python and lies with open mouth across the path of the boys.

working_title: Krishna Kills Aghasura and Revives His Friends
one_line_summary: Entering the demon's throat with his friends, Krishna expands and chokes Aghasura to death, then revives the swallowed boys and calves; the demon's soul merges into Krishna as a great light.

working_title: Brahma Steals the Calves and Boys
one_line_summary: While Krishna searches for the strayed calves, Brahma, wanting to test the Lord, carries off all the calves and cowherd boys and hides them.

working_title: Krishna Expands Into All the Calves and Boys
one_line_summary: To console their mothers, Krishna himself becomes every missing calf and boy, and for a year plays their roles in the cowherd homes.

working_title: Brahma Is Bewildered and Worships Krishna
one_line_summary: Returning after a moment of his time, Brahma finds everything as before and, seeing all the boys as four-armed forms of Vishnu, falls at Krishna's feet in humility.

working_title: Brahma Praises Krishna and Departs
one_line_summary: Brahma hymns Krishna's boundless glories, confesses his own arrogance, and returns to his abode after circumambulating the Lord.

working_title: The Boys Resume Their Meal Unaware of the Lost Year
one_line_summary: Krishna returns the boys and calves as before, and, though a year had passed, to them it seemed but a moment, and they finish their picnic and go home.

working_title: The Boys Long for the Palm Grove's Fruit
one_line_summary: The cowherd boys ask Krishna and Balarama to take them to the talavana, whose sweet fruit is guarded by the donkey-demon Dhenuka.

working_title: Balarama Slays the Ass-Demon Dhenuka
one_line_summary: Balarama shakes the palm trees to bring down the fruit, and when Dhenuka charges, he seizes the donkey and dashes it lifeless against a palm.
variant_notes: BP attributes the deed jointly to Balarama; VP to Rama alone.

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Clear the Grove of Dhenuka's Kin
one_line_summary: As Dhenuka's kin charge to avenge him, Krishna and Balarama slay them all, and men and beasts freely enjoy the grove.

working_title: Krishna Swallows the Forest Fire at Night
one_line_summary: As a forest fire surrounds the sleeping settlement at night, the villagers call on Krishna, who drinks up the fierce flames.

working_title: Pralamba Joins the Games in Disguise
one_line_summary: The demon Pralamba, intent on seizing the boys, joins their play disguised as a cowherd, and Krishna, knowing him, allows it, planning his death.

working_title: Balarama Slays the Demon Pralamba
one_line_summary: In the riding game, Pralamba carries Balarama far off and reveals his terrible form, but Balarama strikes his head with a mighty fist and fells him dead.

working_title: The Cattle Stray Into the Munja Forest and a Wildfire Breaks Out
one_line_summary: While the boys play, the cattle wander into a dense grove of munja grass, and a fierce wildfire springs up around them.

working_title: Krishna Swallows the Wildfire and Saves the Herd
one_line_summary: Krishna bids the terrified cowherds close their eyes, drinks up the flames, and, when they open them, they stand safe at Bhandira.

working_title: Krishna Enjoys the Monsoon Pastures
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter the rain-washed forest with the herd, and the boys share a simple meal of curd-rice with him on a rock.

working_title: The Cowherds Wonder at Krishna's Deeds
one_line_summary: Astonished at Krishna's deeds, the cowherds wonder how a boy could do such things, and Nanda reassures them with Garga's words.
variant_notes: BP adds Nanda recounting Garga's prophecy.

working_title: Nanda Is Seized by Varuna and Rescued
one_line_summary: A servant of Varuna seizes Nanda as he bathes at night; Krishna goes to Varuna's abode and frees him.

working_title: Krishna Reveals His Supreme Abode
one_line_summary: Krishna shows the cowherds his own abode beyond darkness, the eternal Brahman-light.

working_title: Shankhachuda Abducts the Gopis
one_line_summary: As Krishna and Balarama sing in the forest, the demon Shankhachuda carries off the gopis.

working_title: Krishna Slays Shankhachuda and Takes the Jewel
one_line_summary: Krishna overtakes the demon, strikes him dead and gives the crest-jewel to Balarama.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Bull-Demon Arishta
one_line_summary: The bull-demon Arishta terrorizes Vrindavan until Krishna seizes and slays him.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Horse-Demon Keshi
one_line_summary: The horse-demon Keshi attacks, and Krishna thrusts his arm into its mouth until it chokes and dies.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Demon Vyoma
one_line_summary: The demon Vyoma, disguised as a cowherd, carries off boys and seals them in a cave; Krishna slays him and frees them.

working_title: Krishna Resolves to Subdue the Serpent Kaliya
one_line_summary: Finding the Yamuna's lake poisoned by the serpent-king Kaliya, Krishna resolves to leap in and vanquish him.
variant_notes: HV-specific precursor; see 'kaliya_leap'.

working_title: Krishna Revives the Cowherds from Poisoned Water
one_line_summary: Thirsty cowherds and cattle drink the poisoned waters of the Yamuna and die; Krishna revives them all with a glance of nectar.

working_title: Krishna Leaps into Kaliya's Poisoned Pool
one_line_summary: Seeing the Yamuna polluted by the serpent Kaliya's venom, Krishna climbs a kadamba tree and plunges into the deep poisoned pool to subdue him.
variant_notes: VP 5.7 also includes the biting and the despair of the watchers.

working_title: Kaliya Coils Around Krishna and Vraja Despairs
one_line_summary: Kaliya coils around Krishna and holds him motionless in the depths, while the cowherds, cows and all of Gokula rush to the bank in grief.

working_title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya's Heads
one_line_summary: Breaking free of the serpent's coils, Krishna leaps up and dances upon Kaliya's raised heads, trampling each hood that will not bow.
variant_notes: HV/VP fold this dance into the banishment episode (see 'kaliya_banish').

working_title: Kaliya's Wives Plead for His Life
one_line_summary: The serpent's wives, with disheveled hair and folded hands, praise Krishna and beg him to spare their husband's life.

working_title: Krishna Spares and Banishes Kaliya
one_line_summary: Krishna spares Kaliya, orders him to leave the Yamuna for the ocean, and Kaliya departs with his family, leaving the river's waters sweet again.
variant_notes: HV/VP fold in the dance on the hoods; bpc1_035 is Uddhava's recollection.

working_title: Why Kaliya Took Refuge in the Yamuna
one_line_summary: The sage recounts how Kaliya, having withheld Garuda's tribute and been beaten by him, fled to the Yamuna pool, where a curse forbade Garuda to enter.

working_title: Krishna Emerges and the Villagers Rejoice
one_line_summary: Krishna comes out of the pool adorned with gems; the cowherds embrace him, and Nanda gives cattle and gold to the brahmanas for his deliverance.

working_title: Krishna Questions the Indra Sacrifice
one_line_summary: Krishna, bowing humbly, asks Nanda and the elders what ceremony they have begun, its fruit, for whom, and by what means it is accomplished.

working_title: Indra Becomes Furious
one_line_summary: Indra learns his worship has been stopped and grows angry with the cowherds whose lord is Krishna.

working_title: Nanda Explains the Indra Worship
one_line_summary: Nanda explains that Indra, lord of rain, is worshipped with offerings produced by his own showers.

working_title: Krishna Argues for Worshipping Govardhana Hill
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Nanda the cowherds should worship Govardhana hill, the cows and the brahmins rather than Indra.

working_title: The Cowherds Worship Govardhana and Krishna Receives Offerings as the Hill
one_line_summary: Nanda and the cowherds accept Krishna's words and perform the sacrifice to Govardhana hill.
variant_notes: BP splits the worship (10.24) and Krishna's manifestation (10.24) into two beats; VP 5.10 combines them.

working_title: Indra Unleashes the Storm on Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Furious Indra sends the Samvartaka storm-clouds to destroy Nanda's gokula with torrent, hail and wind.

working_title: Krishna Lifts Govardhana Hill
one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Govardhana hill with one hand and holds it aloft like an umbrella to shelter the cowherds.
variant_notes: HV/VP specify seven nights/days; bpc1_036 is Uddhava's recollection.

working_title: Seven Days Beneath Govardhana
one_line_summary: The cowherds shelter beneath the hill for seven days while Krishna holds it, until Indra relents.
variant_notes: Folded into 'govardhana_lift' in HV/VP.

working_title: Krishna Restores the Hill and the Cowherds Rejoice
one_line_summary: Krishna sets the hill back in place; Nanda, Yashoda and Balarama embrace him and the gods rain flowers.

working_title: Indra Surrenders and Begs Forgiveness
one_line_summary: Ashamed Indra approaches Krishna, touches his feet, and asks forgiveness for his pride.

working_title: Indra Installs Krishna as Govinda
one_line_summary: Surabhi the divine cow praises Krishna, and Indra bathes and names him Govinda.

working_title: The Gopis Praise Krishna's Flute
one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute in the forest, and the gopis, describing its sweetness to one another, are carried away into his pastimes.

working_title: The Gopis Perform the Katyayani Vow
one_line_summary: Through the first month of winter, the young gopis bathe in the Yamuna and worship the goddess Katyayani, praying that Krishna become their husband.

working_title: Krishna Steals the Gopis' Clothes
one_line_summary: Krishna carries off the gopis' garments as they bathe, climbs a kadamba tree, and teasingly bids them come and take them back.

working_title: Krishna Returns the Clothes and Blesses the Gopis
one_line_summary: The shivering gopis come from the water, and Krishna, pleased with their sincerity, returns their clothes and promises their wish will be fulfilled.

working_title: The Brahmanas Refuse Krishna's Request for Food
one_line_summary: Hungry, Krishna sends the cowherd boys to ask food of brahmanas performing a sacrifice, but they turn the request away, mistaking Krishna for a mere man.

working_title: The Brahmanas' Wives Bring Food to Krishna
one_line_summary: Krishna then sends the boys to the brahmanas' wives, who, longing for his sight, hasten to him with every kind of food, disregarding their families.

working_title: The Wives Refuse to Return and Krishna Welcomes Them
one_line_summary: The brahmana wives, granted Krishna's sight, refuse to return to their homes, and Krishna, pleased with their devotion, assures them of his grace and sends them back with their minds fixed on him.

working_title: The Brahmanas Repent and Praise Krishna
one_line_summary: Reflecting that their wives' devotion surpassed their own empty rituals, the brahmanas lament their blindness and sing Krishna's praise, longing to see him.

working_title: Krishna Vanishes
one_line_summary: To quell the pride rising in the gopis, Krishna suddenly disappears.

working_title: The Gopis Abandon Their Homes
one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute on an autumn night and the gopis leave homes, husbands and duties to rush to him.

working_title: Krishna Tests the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna tells the gopis to return to their husbands, and they plead that he is their very soul.

working_title: Krishna Relents and Sports with the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna smiles, shows the gopis favor, and enjoys himself with them on the Yamuna's bank.

working_title: The Gopis Search the Forest
one_line_summary: The gopis wander the forest questioning the trees and plants about the vanished Krishna.

working_title: The Gopis Enact Krishna's Lilas
one_line_summary: In their frenzy the gopis imitate Krishna's childhood deeds, each playing a part.

working_title: The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing
one_line_summary: Finding footprints of Krishna and his chosen gopi, the gopis marvel; she grows proud, and Krishna vanishes again.

working_title: Krishna Reappears Among the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna reappears smiling and the gopis rise as if their life had returned; their grief ends.

working_title: Krishna Teaches About Love
one_line_summary: Krishna answers the gopis' question about why he loves those who love him, explaining the ways of love.

working_title: The Great Rasa Dance
one_line_summary: Krishna multiplies himself to dance between every gopi in the moonlit rasa; the gods watch and rain flowers.
variant_notes: bpc1_037 is Uddhava's recollection.

working_title: Uddhava Arrives Bearing Krishna's Message
one_line_summary: Uddhava arrives in Vrindavan as Krishna's envoy; the gopis, pining for Krishna, surround him and ask why he has come.

working_title: The Gopi's Lament to the Bee (Bhramara-gita)
one_line_summary: A gopi, seeing a honeybee, addresses it as Krishna's messenger and reproaches Krishna for abandoning the gopis.

working_title: Uddhava Delivers Krishna's Message and the Gopis Reply
one_line_summary: Uddhava conveys Krishna's teaching of unbroken spiritual union; the gopis answer that they cannot forget Krishna.

working_title: Uddhava Praises the Gopis and Departs
one_line_summary: Uddhava extols the gopis' supreme devotion, wishes to be a shrub in Vrindavan, stays some months, then returns to Mathura.

working_title: Akrura Journeys to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: On the road Akrura, filled with devotion, ponders what merit has earned him the sight of Krishna.

working_title: Akrura Arrives in Vrindavan and Beholds Krishna
one_line_summary: Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama, prostrates, and is honored by Nanda with food and questions.

working_title: Akrura Reveals Kamsa's Plan and Krishna Agrees to Go
one_line_summary: Krishna questions Akrura, who tells him of Kamsa's enmity and the purpose of his mission.
variant_notes: VP 5.18 has Krishna vow to slay Kansa within three nights.

working_title: The Gopis Grieve at Krishna's Departure
one_line_summary: When Nanda proclaims the journey to Mathura, the gopis lament that Akrura is taking Krishna away.

working_title: Krishna Consoles the Gopis
one_line_summary: As the chariot leaves, Krishna promises the weeping gopis that he will return.

working_title: Akrura Beholds the Divine Vision in the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Diving in the Yamuna, Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama as the Lord resting on Shesha surrounded by gods.

working_title: Akrura Reports to Kamsa
one_line_summary: Krishna withdraws the divine vision; Akrura drives on and reports to Kamsa before going home.

working_title: Nanda Departs for Vraja
one_line_summary: Krishna embraces Nanda, bids him return to Vraja, and Nanda departs in tears with the cowherds.

working_title: Kamsa Orders the Gopas Expelled and Vasudeva Punished
one_line_summary: Seeing his wrestlers slain, Kansa orders the cowherds expelled, Nanda bound, and Vasudeva punished; Krishna grows wrathful.
variant_notes: HV-specific; the provocation immediately preceding the killing (see 'slay_kamsa').

working_title: Garuda Restores Vishnu's Stolen Crown to Krishna
one_line_summary: Garuda, having recovered Vishnu's crown stolen by Bali's son, places it on Krishna's head on Gomanta.

working_title: Krishna Returns to Mathura
one_line_summary: Rama and Krishna, accompanied by Damaghosha, enter Mathura and are received with joy by Ugrasena and the Yadavas before honoring their parents.

working_title: Kaishika Offers His Kingdom
one_line_summary: The Vidarbha kings Kratha and Kaishika offer Krishna their kingdom and arrange his consecration, while a celestial voice announces that Indra has sent a golden seat.

working_title: Krishna's Royal Consecration
one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, celestial jars pour sacred water and Indra himself adorns Krishna, completing the Abhisheka ceremony of his imperial consecration.

working_title: Ugrasena Welcomes Krishna Back
one_line_summary: Krishna returns to Mathura, where Ugrasena comes out to honor him; Krishna declines the royal arghya and reaffirms Ugrasena as king, then consoles him over Kamsa's death.

working_title: Krishna Obtains the Celestial Hall Sudharman
one_line_summary: Krishna bids Vayu ask Indra to resign the splendid hall Sudharman; Indra yields it, and the Yadava chiefs thenceforth possess the jewel-adorned celestial court.
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Sudharman-hall motif: Vishnu Purana 5.21 tells the fetching of the celestial hall for Ugrasena at Mathura; Harivamsha 1.115 folds the same hall into the enrichment of Dwaraka. Different placement — kept separate.

working_title: Narada Reveals the Truth to Kamsa
one_line_summary: Narada tells Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama are the sons of Devaki and Rohini; Kamsa binds Vasudeva and Devaki.

working_title: Kamsa Orders the Wrestlers and Elephant to Kill Krishna
one_line_summary: Kamsa summons Chanura and Mushtika and orders Krishna and Balarama killed by wrestling and by the elephant Kuvalayapida.

working_title: Kamsa Sends Akrura to Fetch Krishna
one_line_summary: Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sends him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama to Mathura.
variant_notes: VP 5.15 also folds in the sending of Kesin.

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Enter Mathura
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter Mathura with the cowherds, and the city's women throng to see them.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Insolent Washerman
one_line_summary: The king's washerman refuses Krishna clothes and abuses him; Krishna strikes off his head and takes the garments.

working_title: Krishna Straightens the Hunchback Kubja
one_line_summary: Kubja gives Krishna sandal paste, and he straightens her crooked body into a beautiful woman.

working_title: Krishna Breaks Kamsa's Great Bow
one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Kamsa's great bow and breaks it, then strikes down the attacking guards.

working_title: Kamsa Is Terrified by Evil Omens
one_line_summary: Kamsa, hearing of the bow's breaking, spends a sleepless night beset by omens and dreams of death.

working_title: Kamsa Orders the Wrestling Festival
one_line_summary: At dawn Kamsa orders the wrestling festival; the arena is prepared and the cowherds arrive with offerings.

working_title: Krishna Slays the Elephant Kuvalayapida
one_line_summary: At the arena gate Krishna evades the elephant Kuvalayapida, throws it down, tears out its tusk and slays it.

working_title: The Citizens Rejoice in the Arena
one_line_summary: Entering with the tusk as weapon, Krishna delights the people, who recount his deeds as Narayana and Rama.

working_title: Chanura Challenges Krishna and Balarama
one_line_summary: Chanura invites Krishna and Balarama to wrestle; Krishna answers that they are boys, but Chanura insists.

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Slay the Wrestlers
one_line_summary: Despite the women's protest, Krishna slays Chanura and Balarama slays Mushtika, Kuta, Shala and Tośala.

working_title: Krishna Slays Kamsa
one_line_summary: As Kamsa orders Nanda bound and Vasudeva killed, Krishna leaps onto the dais, seizes and slays him.
variant_notes: bpc1_038 is Uddhava's recollection.

working_title: Balarama Slays Kamsa's Brothers
one_line_summary: Kamsa's eight brothers rush at Krishna in fury and Balarama slays them all with his club.
variant_notes: HV folds in the greeting of the parents.

working_title: Kamsa's Wives Lament and the Funeral Rites Are Performed
one_line_summary: The wives of the slain warriors weep, and Krishna comforts them and has the funeral rites performed.

working_title: Krishna Frees and Bows to Vasudeva and Devaki
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama release their parents from bonds and bow, touching their feet.

working_title: Krishna Begs His Parents' Forgiveness
one_line_summary: Krishna humbly begs Vasudeva and Devaki's forgiveness for having been unable to serve them.

working_title: Krishna Installs Ugrasena as King
one_line_summary: Krishna makes his grandfather Ugrasena king of the Yadavas, honoring Yayati's curse.
variant_notes: VP 5.21 also folds in the consolation of the widows.

working_title: Krishna Restores the Yadava Kinsmen
one_line_summary: Krishna brings back and settles all the Yadava kinsmen who had fled in fear of Kamsa.

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Study Under Sandipani
one_line_summary: The two brothers are initiated and go to the teacher Sandipani, mastering all arts in sixty-four days.
variant_notes: See 'sandipani_son' (VP 5.21 combines study + recovery).

working_title: Krishna Retrieves Sandipani's Son
one_line_summary: As teacher's fee, Krishna slays Panchajana, takes his conch, and brings Sandipani's dead son back from Yama's city.
variant_notes: VP 5.21 folds in the study; bpc1_039 is Uddhava's recollection.

working_title: Krishna Visits Trivakra and Grants Her a Boon
one_line_summary: Krishna visits the hunchback woman Trivakra, accepts her hospitality, and grants her a boon, honoring her devotion.
variant_notes: Later visit (10.48); see 'kubja_straighten' for the first meeting.

working_title: Memories of the Gurukula || Krishna and Sudama recall their student days under Sandipani, when they were sent to fetch firewood and, caught in a fierce storm, wandered lost until the guru found them at dawn.
one_line_summary: Krishna and Sudama recall their student days under Sandipani, when they were sent to fetch firewood and, caught in a fierce storm, wandered lost until the guru found them at dawn.

working_title: The Yadavas Counsel That Mathura Cannot Withstand Siege
one_line_summary: The Yadavas tell Krishna that Mathura lacks walls and provisions and cannot withstand Jarasandha's repeated sieges.

working_title: Krishna Resolves to Abandon Mathura
one_line_summary: Krishna decides to leave Mathura with Balarama and head south, to draw Jarasandha away and protect the city.

working_title: Krishna Meets Parasurama, Who Counsels Gomanta
one_line_summary: On mount Sahya, Krishna meets the sage Parasurama, who counsels him to make his stand against Jarasandha on mount Gomanta.

working_title: Krishna Wields the Divine Weapons on Gomanta
one_line_summary: On Gomanta, the divine weapons descend to Krishna and Balarama, who rout the kings; Balarama slays king Darada.

working_title: The King of Chedi Befriends Krishna and Escorts Him to Karavira
one_line_summary: After Jarasandha flees, the king of Chedi, Krishna's kinsman by marriage, befriends him and escorts him to the city of Karavira.

working_title: Krishna Installs Shakradeva on the Throne of Karavira
one_line_summary: At the plea of Shrigala's queen, Krishna installs the slain king's son Shakradeva on the throne of Karavira.

working_title: Jarasandha Warns the Assembled Kings
one_line_summary: At Bhishmaka's council Jarasandha warns the assembled kings that Krishna is Vishnu himself, whose arrival for the maiden spells calamity; Sunitha concurs.

working_title: The Kings Debate and Bhishmaka Yields
one_line_summary: Dantavakra urges peace with Krishna while Salwa scorns fear; Bhishmaka, fearing for his arrogant son Rukmi, resolves to go and propitiate Krishna.

working_title: Shalya Proposes Inviting Kalayavana
one_line_summary: Shalya tells the kings that Kalayavana, whom no prince of Mathura can slay by Rudra's boon, should be invited against Krishna; Jarasandha dispatches Shalya as envoy.

working_title: Shalya Delivers Jarasandha's Message to Kalayavana
one_line_summary: Shalya arrives at Kalayavana's court, recounts the destruction at Gomanta and Jarasandha's plea, and urges Kalayavana to march on Mathura.

working_title: Kalayavana Marches on Mathura
one_line_summary: Kalayavana, elated by the kings' request, honors Shalya and sets out that very day with his army to vanquish Krishna.
variant_notes: VP 5.23 gives Gargya's penance as Kalayavana's origin; HV has Shalya invite him.

working_title: The Serpent-Jar Stratagem Against Kalayavana
one_line_summary: As Kalayavana advances, Krishna sends him a sealed jar holding a black serpent as a warning; Kalayavana answers by filling the jar with ants that devour it.

working_title: Jarasandha Hurls His Mace toward Mathura
one_line_summary: Enraged by Kansa's death, Jarasandha whirls a mace ninety-nine times and hurls it toward Mathura where Krishna lives; the citizens inform Krishna of its fall.

working_title: Krishna Proposes Slaying Jarasandha as Prelude to the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: Krishna counsels that Jarasandha, unbeatable in battle by gods and asuras, must be slain in a bare-armed personal struggle, assigning policy to himself, strength to Bhima, and triumph to Arjuna.
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Rajasuya slaying-plan: Mahabharata attributes the proposal to Krishna himself; Bhagavata Purana 10.71 presents the same plan as Uddhava's counsel to Krishna. Attribution difference is material — kept as separate stories.

working_title: Krishna and the Pandavas Break the Chaityaka Peak
one_line_summary: Entering Girivraja not by the gate but by piercing the sacred Chaityaka peak, Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna break down the celebrated hill worshipped by the Magadhas.

working_title: Krishna Speaks for the Silent Disguised Brothers
one_line_summary: Received by Jarasandha, Krishna explains that his two companions observe a vow of silence until midnight, so he alone speaks for the disguised trio.

working_title: Krishna Answers Jarasandha's Challenge about the Disguise
one_line_summary: When Jarasandha censures the disguised guests for entering by an improper gate, Krishna replies that a foe's abode is entered by the wrong gate and the foe's hospitality is refused.

working_title: Krishna Refrains from Slaying Jarasandha
one_line_summary: Remembering Brahma's command that Jarasandha is destined to die at Bhima's hands, Krishna withholds his own hand and leaves the king to Bhima.

working_title: Krishna Seizes Kalayavana's Host || Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.
one_line_summary: Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.

working_title: Jarasandha Attacks and Besieges Mathura
one_line_summary: Kamsa's widows report to Jarasandha, who vows to destroy the Yadavas and besieges Mathura with twenty-three armies.
variant_notes: VP 5.22 folds in the routing of Jarasandha across eighteen attacks; HV splits the march (1.89) and the siege (1.90).

working_title: A Divine Chariot and Weapons Descend for Krishna
one_line_summary: As Krishna deliberates, a divine chariot and celestial weapons descend from the sky; Krishna and Balarama ride out to battle.

working_title: The Yadavas Rout Jarasandha's Army and Spare Him
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama annihilate Jarasandha's host; Balarama seizes Jarasandha, but Krishna releases him to fight again.
variant_notes: HV splits the battle and the divine voice sparing Jarasandha.

working_title: Kalayavana Is Burned by Muchukunda's Glance
one_line_summary: Krishna lures Kalayavana into Muchukunda's cave; the Yavana kicks the sleeping king and is reduced to ashes.

working_title: Muchukunda's Story || Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.
one_line_summary: Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.
variant_notes: BP-only beat; immediately precedes the boon (bp10c_015).

working_title: Krishna Grants Muchukunda His Boon || Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.
one_line_summary: Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.
variant_notes: BP-only beat; follows Muchukunda's story (bp10c_014).

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Elude Jarasandha || Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Harivamsha resolve to abandon Mathura (hv_a_001) and the founding (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02).

working_title: The Captive Kings Appeal to Krishna || A royal messenger arrives in Krishna's assembly and reports that Jarasandha has imprisoned twenty thousand defeated kings in Girivraja, who beg Krishna for release.
one_line_summary: A royal messenger arrives in Krishna's assembly and reports that Jarasandha has imprisoned twenty thousand defeated kings in Girivraja, who beg Krishna for release.
characters: Krishna; Jarasandha; the captive kings; royal messenger

working_title: Uddhava's Counsel to Slay Jarasandha || Uddhava advises Krishna that the Rajasuya requires conquering the directions, and that Jarasandha — who can only be killed by Bhima in single combat — must first be destroyed.
one_line_summary: Uddhava advises Krishna that the Rajasuya requires conquering the directions, and that Jarasandha — who can only be killed by Bhima in single combat — must first be destroyed.
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Rajasuya slaying-plan: Bhagavata Purana attributes the plan to Uddhava's counsel; Mahabharata 2.20 presents Krishna himself proposing it. Attribution difference is material — kept as separate stories.

working_title: Krishna's Grand Procession from Dwaraka || Krishna departs Dwaraka for Indraprastha with a vast army, chariots, elephants and his queens, to the sound of drums and conches.
one_line_summary: Krishna departs Dwaraka for Indraprastha with a vast army, chariots, elephants and his queens, to the sound of drums and conches.

working_title: Sahadeva Crowned and the Kings Freed || Krishna crowns Jarasandha's son Sahadeva king of Magadha and releases all the kings imprisoned by Jarasandha.
one_line_summary: Krishna crowns Jarasandha's son Sahadeva king of Magadha and releases all the kings imprisoned by Jarasandha.

working_title: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna Approach Jarasandha in Disguise
one_line_summary: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna travel to Girivraja disguised as brahmanas and ask Jarasandha for alms, testing his charity.

working_title: Krishna Reveals Their Identities and Challenges Jarasandha
one_line_summary: Krishna reveals their true identities and asks for single combat; Jarasandha laughs, taunts Krishna as a coward who fled Mathura, and chooses Bhima as his opponent.

working_title: The Mace-Duel of Bhima and Jarasandha || Bhima and Jarasandha fight an indecisive mace-duel, exchanging blows that crush their clubs, then striking with iron-hard fists.
one_line_summary: Bhima and Jarasandha fight an indecisive mace-duel, exchanging blows that crush their clubs, then striking with iron-hard fists.

working_title: Krishna's Signal: Jarasandha Split in Two || Knowing Jarasandha's birth secret, Krishna signals by splitting a twig; Bhima tears Jarasandha in two and kills him.
one_line_summary: Knowing Jarasandha's birth secret, Krishna signals by splitting a twig; Bhima tears Jarasandha in two and kills him.

working_title: The Liberated Kings Behold Krishna || Twenty thousand eight hundred freed kings emerge from the mountain prison, behold Krishna's form, praise him, receive his teaching, and are sent home with honor.
one_line_summary: Twenty thousand eight hundred freed kings emerge from the mountain prison, behold Krishna's form, praise him, receive his teaching, and are sent home with honor.
characters: Krishna; the twenty thousand kings; Sahadeva

working_title: Krishna Selects the Site of Dwaraka || The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.
one_line_summary: The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02); site-selection beat.

working_title: Krishna Enriches Dwaraka || Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.
one_line_summary: Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster; enrichment beat.

working_title: Vishwakarma Adorns Dwarka for Krishna || At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.
one_line_summary: At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.

working_title: Viswakarma Builds Dwaraka for Krishna
one_line_summary: Facing Kalayavana and Jarasandha together, Krishna builds the fortress-city of Dvaraka in the sea and relocates the Yadavas.

working_title: News of Rukmini's Swayamvara
one_line_summary: Spies inform Krishna that Rukmini, sister of Rukmi, will hold her swayamvara at Kundina; Krishna sets out with the Yadava army, bidding Ugrasena guard Mathura.

working_title: Krishna Summons Garuda at Bhishmaka's House
one_line_summary: Arriving at Bhishmaka's house for the swayamvara, Krishna thinks of Garuda to overawe the assembled kings, and the bird-king appears, shaking the earth with his wings.

working_title: Krishna Reveals Rukmini Is Lakshmi
one_line_summary: In dialogue with Bhishmaka, Krishna declares that Rukmini is the goddess Lakshmi born to be his wife and should not be given away in a public swayamvara.

working_title: Bhishmaka Beholds Krishna's Cosmic Form
one_line_summary: Krishna takes leave of Bhishmaka, who beholds his universal form of a thousand heads and arms and worships him with a eulogy before the kings follow him out.

working_title: Rukmini Declares She Weds Only Krishna
one_line_summary: After the kings disperse, Rukmini tells her friends that she will accept no husband but the lotus-eyed Krishna.

working_title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini and Wins Satya || Uddhava recalls how Krishna carried off Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, by the gandharva rite, and how he defeated the proud kings to win Satya (Nagnajiti) at her svayamvara.
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna carried off Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, by the gandharva rite, and how he defeated the proud kings to win Satya (Nagnajiti) at her svayamvara.
variant_notes: Recall bundling Rukmini's abduction + Satya's svayamvara; cross-ref both clusters.

working_title: Rukmini Resolves to Marry Krishna and Sends a Brahmana Messenger || Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.
one_line_summary: Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01); message is bp10c_018.

working_title: Rukmini's Love-Message to Krishna || Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.
one_line_summary: Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; resolve is bp10c_017.

working_title: Krishna Hastens to Kundina || Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.
one_line_summary: Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01).

working_title: Rukmini's Prayer at the Temple of Ambika || Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.
one_line_summary: Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; distinct prayer beat.

working_title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini
one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Rukmini as she leaves the temple, places her on his chariot, and rides off before the assembled kings.
variant_notes: BP 10.53 seizes her at the svayamvara after her temple prayer; VP 5.26 carries her off on the eve of her betrothal to Sisupala.

working_title: Krishna Defeats and Spares Rukmi
one_line_summary: Krishna's forces rout the pursuing kings; Rukmi chases alone, and Krishna defeats and disfigures him but spares his life at Rukmini's entreaty.
variant_notes: Harivamsha 1.116 has Rukmi vow to slay Krishna then duel near the Narmada; VP/BP have him pursue and be spared at Rukmini's plea.

working_title: Krishna Marries Rukmini
one_line_summary: Rukmi founds the city of Bhojakata, and Krishna formally weds Rukmini in Dvaraka amid citywide celebration.
variant_notes: VP 5.26 bundles Pradyumna's birth with the marriage; Harivamsha notes Rukmini as first wife and mother of ten sons.

working_title: Krishna Weds Kalindi at the Yamuna
one_line_summary: While hunting with Arjuna, Krishna meets Kalindi, daughter of the Sun, doing penance at the Yamuna, and later weds her.

working_title: Krishna Abducts Mitravinda and Wins Satya || Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.
one_line_summary: Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.
variant_notes: Bundles two moments (Mitravinda + Satya); cross-ref bpc1_040 for the Satya recall.

working_title: Krishna Jests with Rukmini || Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.
one_line_summary: Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.
variant_notes: BP-only; paired with consolation beat (bp10c_049).

working_title: Krishna Consoles Rukmini || Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.
one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.
variant_notes: BP-only; paired with jest beat (bp10c_048).

working_title: Balarama Slays Rukmi at the Dice Game
one_line_summary: At the wedding, Rukmi cheats Balarama at dice and insults him; enraged, Balarama kills Rukmi with his iron club.
variant_notes: Weapon varies: iron club (BP), dice-board (Harivamsha). VP adds a heavenly voice confirms the foul play.

working_title: Krishna Wins Lakshmana at Her Svayamvara
one_line_summary: Krishna weds Bhadra, daughter of his aunt, and carries off Lakshmana of Madra from her svayamvara.
variant_notes: bp10d_039 gives Lakshmana's own account (strung a bow, shot the fish target); bp10c_040 bundles her abduction with Bhadra's marriage.

working_title: The Vrishnis Suspect Krishna of Stealing the Jewel || Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.
one_line_summary: Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Prasena cluster (bp10c_029/hv_a_003); distinct accusation beat.

working_title: Balarama Departs to Mithila in Anger || Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.
one_line_summary: Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_034/hv_a_008).

working_title: Akrura's Exile Brings Drought; His Return Brings Rain || After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.
one_line_summary: After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.
variant_notes: Harivamsha-only; Akrura's exile/drought episode.

working_title: Surya Grants Satrajit the Syamantaka Jewel
one_line_summary: Surya gives his devotee Satrajit the Syamantaka jewel, which yields eight loads of gold daily and makes him shine like the sun.
variant_notes: BP: jewel yields eight loads of gold daily; Harivamsha: Satrajit worships the sun on the ocean bank.

working_title: Prasena Is Slain by a Lion for the Jewel
one_line_summary: Satrajit refuses to hand the jewel to Krishna; his brother Prasena, wearing it on a hunt, is killed by a lion, and rumor blames Krishna.
variant_notes: BP 10.56 bundles Satrajit's refusal and the rumor blaming Krishna into the same beat; Harivamsha adds Jambavan killing the lion and taking the jewel.

working_title: Krishna Wrestles Jambavan for the Jewel
one_line_summary: To clear his name, Krishna traces Prasena's path, enters Jambavan's cave, and fights the bear-king for twenty-eight days before Jambavan yields the jewel and his daughter.
variant_notes: Duration varies: twenty-eight days (BP) vs twenty-one days (Harivamsha).

working_title: Krishna Returns the Jewel and Clears His Name
one_line_summary: Krishna returns with the jewel and Jambavati, clears his name in open assembly, and returns the Syamantaka to Satrajit, who also offers Satyabhama.
variant_notes: BP has him clear his name in open assembly and also receive Satyabhama.

working_title: Satadhanva Murders Satrajit for the Jewel
one_line_summary: Instigated by Akrura and Kritavarma, Satadhanva murders the sleeping Satrajit and steals the Syamantaka jewel.
variant_notes: Harivamsha adds that Shatadhanwa secretly gives the jewel to Akrura; BP notes instigation by Akrura and Kritavarma.

working_title: Satyabhama Reports Her Father's Murder || Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.
one_line_summary: Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_032/hv_a_007).

working_title: Krishna Pursues and Slays Satadhanva
one_line_summary: Krishna pursues and beheads Satadhanva near Mithila but finds no jewel; Balarama goes on to visit King Janaka.
variant_notes: Both: killed near Mithila, no jewel found.

working_title: Krishna Reclaims the Jewel from Akrura
one_line_summary: Krishna reveals that Satadhanva had left the jewel with Akrura; Akrura produces it, and Krishna returns it to him after showing it to his kinsmen.
variant_notes: Both have Krishna discern the jewel is with Akrura and return it to him after showing it in assembly.

working_title: Indra Reports Naraka's Tyranny and Asks Krishna's Help
one_line_summary: Indra descends to Dwaraka, recounts how the demon Naraka stole Aditi's ear-rings, and asks Krishna to slay him; Krishna departs with Satyabhama on Garuda.
variant_notes: VP lists Naraka's thefts (maidens, Varuna's umbrella, Aditi's earrings, demands Indra's elephant); Harivamsha has Indra descend and Krishna depart with Satyabhama on Garuda.

working_title: Narada Presents the Parijata Flower to Rukmini || Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.
one_line_summary: Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.

working_title: Satyabhama Is Consumed by Jealousy || Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.
one_line_summary: Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.

working_title: Krishna Consoles the Jealous Satyabhama || Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.
one_line_summary: Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.

working_title: Krishna Promises Satyabhama the Parijata Tree || Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.
one_line_summary: Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.

working_title: Krishna Sends Narada to Ask Indra for the Parijata || Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.
one_line_summary: Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.

working_title: Indra Refuses and Challenges Krishna || Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.
one_line_summary: Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.

working_title: Indra and the Gods Contend with Krishna over the Parijata
one_line_summary: The garden-keepers alert Indra, who rides out on Airavata and demands Krishna return the Parijata, challenging him to battle for it.
locations: Nandana forest; eastern gate of heaven
variant_notes: VP: Krishna disarms all the gods with his discus and spares Indra; Harivamsha: Indra rides Airavata and challenges Krishna to battle.

working_title: Satyaki Fights the Brahmana Pravara; Garuda Strikes Him Down || Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.
one_line_summary: Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.

working_title: Garuda Fells Airavata from Heaven || Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.
one_line_summary: Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.

working_title: Krishna Worships Shiva and Wins His Boon || Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.
one_line_summary: Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.

working_title: Shiva Reveals the Danava Stronghold of Satpura || Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.
one_line_summary: Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.

working_title: Krishna Brings the Parijata to Satyabhama in Dvaraka
one_line_summary: Aditi grants Krishna the Parijata for Satyabhama's rite on condition of its return; Krishna plants it at Raivataka and carries it into Dwarka, where Satyabhama receives it joyfully.
variant_notes: Harivamsha: Aditi grants it on condition of return; VP: planted in Satyabhama's garden.

working_title: Kashyapa and Aditi Reconcile Krishna and Indra || Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.
one_line_summary: Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.

working_title: Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite and the Gift to Narada || Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.
one_line_summary: Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.

working_title: Krishna Returns the Parijata and Vows to Destroy the Danavas || After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.
one_line_summary: After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.

working_title: The Danavas Demand a Share of Brahmadatta's Yajna || At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.
one_line_summary: At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.

working_title: Narada Incites the Kings to Aid the Asuras || Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.
one_line_summary: Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.

working_title: Nikumbha Imprisons the Yadava Heroes by Maya || Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.
one_line_summary: Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.

working_title: Krishna Routs the Asuras with the Sarnga Bow || Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.
one_line_summary: Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.

working_title: Krishna Distributes the Spoils and Grants Shatpura to Brahmadatta || After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.
one_line_summary: After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.

working_title: Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas || Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.
one_line_summary: Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.
characters: Krishna; Narada; Arjuna; Rambha; Urvashi; Pradyumna

working_title: Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus || As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.
one_line_summary: As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.

working_title: Vajranabha Wins His Boon and Demands the Three Worlds || By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.
one_line_summary: By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.

working_title: The Yadavas Enter Vajra Disguised as Actors || Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.
one_line_summary: Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.

working_title: Kashyapa Warns Vajranabha, Who Marches on Heaven || After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.
one_line_summary: After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.

working_title: Krishna Returns to Dwarka and Honors Naraka's Captive Maidens || Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.
one_line_summary: Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.

working_title: Jvara Consumes Baladeva; Krishna Saves Him || The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.
one_line_summary: The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.

working_title: Krishna Grapples with Jvara || Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.
one_line_summary: Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.

working_title: Jvara Possesses Krishna; Krishna Expels Him || The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.
one_line_summary: The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.

working_title: Krishna Spares Jvara and Grants Him Boons || Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.
one_line_summary: Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.

working_title: Shiva and Kartikeya Enter the Battle for Vana || As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.
one_line_summary: As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.
themes: divine intervention; ghostly host; protecting Vana

working_title: Kottavi Intervenes to Save Kartikeya || As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.
one_line_summary: As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.

working_title: Vana Vaunts and Fights Krishna || Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.
one_line_summary: Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.

working_title: Kottavi Again Intercedes; Krishna Vows to Cut Vana's Arms || When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.
one_line_summary: When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.

working_title: Shiva Intercedes for Vana; Vana Dances and Wins Boons || Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.
one_line_summary: Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.

working_title: Krishna Fights Varuna for the Celestial Cows || Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.
one_line_summary: Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.
characters: Krishna; Varuna; Garuda; Baladeva; Pradyumna; Aniruddha

working_title: Varuna Pleads His Promise; Krishna Relents || Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.
one_line_summary: Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.

working_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura and Weds the Sixteen Thousand || Uddhava recalls how Krishna slew the demon Naraka (Bhauma), who had seized the earth's princesses, and how the freed princesses chose Krishna as their husband, who married them all in one moment and begot sons in each.
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna slew the demon Naraka (Bhauma), who had seized the earth's princesses, and how the freed princesses chose Krishna as their husband, who married them all in one moment and begot sons in each.
characters: Krishna; Narakasura (Bhauma); the sixteen thousand princesses
themes: liberation of the captives; marriage; the demon slain
variant_notes: Recall bundling Naraka's slaying + the 16,000 marriages; cross-ref both clusters.

working_title: Krishna Restores Aditi's Earrings || Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.
one_line_summary: Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Parijata-uprooting cluster (bp10c_046 etc.); VP's separate earrings-restoration beat.

working_title: Krishna Breaches Mura's Fortifications || Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.
one_line_summary: Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster; distinct fortification-breach beat (Mura's defenses).

working_title: Krishna Slays Mura and His Seven Sons || Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.
one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster (hv_b1_120_02 bundles Mura's slaying).

working_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura
one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the demon king Narakasura (Bhauma) with his discus, freeing the three worlds of his tyranny.
variant_notes: Method: discus behead (BP), cut in two with discus (Harivamsha), cut nooses then slay (VP).

working_title: Bhumi Returns Aditi's Earrings || The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.
one_line_summary: The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.
variant_notes: Distinct: Bhumi (earth-goddess) restores the treasures; cross-ref Krishna's earrings restoration (vp5_030_01).

working_title: Krishna Frees the Sixteen Thousand Captive Maidens
one_line_summary: Krishna enters Narakasura's palace and frees the 16,100 captive princesses, who all choose him as their husband.
variant_notes: Both: sixteen thousand maidens choose Krishna as husband.

working_title: Krishna Uproots the Parijata Tree from Indra's Heaven
one_line_summary: Krishna returns Aditi's earrings to the gods, and at Satyabhama's wish uproots the Parijata tree from Indra's heaven, defeating the gods.
variant_notes: BP 10.59 and Harivamsha 1.121 bundle the restoration of Aditi's earrings with the uprooting; bpc1_041 is Uddhava's recall.

working_title: Krishna Marries the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
one_line_summary: Krishna, expanding into as many forms, simultaneously weds the 16,100 princesses, giving each a palace and household.
variant_notes: Both: Krishna multiplies into 16,100 forms so each wife believes him hers alone.

working_title: Krishna Shields Parikshit in Uttara's Womb
one_line_summary: As Krishna departs Hastinapura, the terrified Uttara cries for protection from Ashvatthama's weapon; Krishna enters her womb by his yoga-maya and shields the unborn Parikshit with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.

working_title: Krishna Slays King Shrigala with the Discus
one_line_summary: King Shrigala of Karavira attacks Krishna, who slays him with the Sudarshana discus.

working_title: Krishna Slays Nikumbha with the Sudarshana Discus || As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.
one_line_summary: As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.

working_title: Nikumbha Carries Away Bhanumati || While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.
one_line_summary: While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.

working_title: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna Pursue the Abductor || Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.
one_line_summary: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.
locations: on the way; mount Gokarna; river Chela Ganga

working_title: Narada Reveals Bhanumati's Fate; She Weds Sahadeva || Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.
one_line_summary: Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.

working_title: Krishna Shatters the Rock-Shower with Indra's Thunderbolt || Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.
one_line_summary: Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.

working_title: Krishna Seizes His Discus and Charges Bhishma
one_line_summary: Unable to bear Bhishma's slaughter of the Pandava army, Krishna abandons the chariot reins, leaps down with the discus Sudarshana, and rushes impetuously toward Bhishma to slay him.

working_title: Nanda Is Swallowed by a Serpent and Freed
one_line_summary: A great serpent swallows Nanda as he sleeps; Krishna's touch frees the cursed Vidyadhara Sudarshana.

working_title: The Weaver and Sudama (Flower-Seller) Honor Krishna
one_line_summary: A weaver dresses Krishna and Balarama, and the garland-maker Sudama honors them and receives a boon.
variant_notes: BP adds the weaver; VP has only the flower-seller.

working_title: Krishna Liberates King Nriga from a Lizard's Body || The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.
one_line_summary: The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.
variant_notes: BP-only; Nriga episode has no cross-source parallel in this chunk.

working_title: Nriga's Story of the Disputed Cow || Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.
one_line_summary: Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.
variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_060.

working_title: Nriga Ascends and Krishna Warns Against Stealing Brahmanas' Wealth || Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.
