one_line_summary: Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.
variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_061.

working_title: Paundraka Falsely Claims to Be Vasudeva || Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.
one_line_summary: Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Paundraka-slaying cluster (bp10c_066/vp5_034_01).

working_title: Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi
one_line_summary: Krishna marches to Kashi, beheads the impostor Paundraka with his discus, and casts the head of the Kashi king into his own city.
variant_notes: Both: impostor Paundraka beheaded, Kashi king's head cast/shot into his own city.

working_title: Sudarshana Consumes the Conjured Fire and Burns Varanasi/Benares
one_line_summary: Sudakshina conjures a fiery demon by black magic to kill Krishna; Krishna's Sudarshana discus destroys it and burns Varanasi.
variant_notes: BP: Sudakshina conjures the fiery demon; VP: the son of the slain Kashi king conjures the fiend.

working_title: Samba Carries Off Duryodhana's Daughter
one_line_summary: Samba carries off Lakshmana, Duryodhana's daughter, from her svayamvara; the Kauravas fight him and take him captive.
variant_notes: Both: Samba abducts her at the svayamvara and is captured by the Kuru chiefs.

working_title: Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka || Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.
one_line_summary: Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.

working_title: Narada Marvels at Krishna's Yoga-Maya and Departs || Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.
one_line_summary: Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.

working_title: Krishna's Dawn Worship in Dwaraka || Krishna rises in the brahma-muhurta, performs his ablutions, worships the Lord within, gives daily gifts of cows and wealth to brahmanas, and blesses his people.
one_line_summary: Krishna rises in the brahma-muhurta, performs his ablutions, worships the Lord within, gives daily gifts of cows and wealth to brahmanas, and blesses his people.

working_title: Sudama's Poverty and Journey || Sudama's wife urges the destitute brahmana to seek his boyhood friend Krishna, and he sets out for Dwaraka with a humble gift of flat rice.
one_line_summary: Sudama's wife urges the destitute brahmana to seek his boyhood friend Krishna, and he sets out for Dwaraka with a humble gift of flat rice.

working_title: Krishna Embraces His Old Friend || Krishna rises from his couch, embraces Sudama with tears of joy, washes his feet, and anoints him, while Rukmini fans him, astonishing the palace women.
one_line_summary: Krishna rises from his couch, embraces Sudama with tears of joy, washes his feet, and anoints him, while Rukmini fans him, astonishing the palace women.

working_title: Krishna Eats Sudama's Flat Rice || Krishna asks for the gift and eats Sudama's handful of flat rice with delight, and Sudama, too ashamed to ask for anything, returns home empty-handed.
one_line_summary: Krishna asks for the gift and eats Sudama's handful of flat rice with delight, and Sudama, too ashamed to ask for anything, returns home empty-handed.

working_title: Sudama Finds His Hut a Palace || Returning home, Sudama finds his poor dwelling transformed into a celestial palace and his wife radiant, and he reflects that this is Krishna's unasked grace.
one_line_summary: Returning home, Sudama finds his poor dwelling transformed into a celestial palace and his wife radiant, and he reflects that this is Krishna's unasked grace.

working_title: Vasudeva's Sacrifice
one_line_summary: The sages, pleased with Vasudeva's question, initiate him and he performs a great sacrifice at Samanta-panchaka, with his sons and the Yadavas attending.
characters: Vasudeva; Krishna; Balarama; Narada; the sages

working_title: Devaki Asks for Her Slain Sons
one_line_summary: Devaki, remembering the six sons Kamsa killed, tearfully asks Krishna and Balarama to bring back her dead children.

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Visit Bali in Sutala
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama descend to Sutala, where Bali, the daitya king, receives them with great devotion, and Krishna reveals the true origin of Devaki's six sons.
themes: descent to the underworld; devotion; revelation

working_title: The Six Sons Restored to Devaki
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama bring the six sons back from Sutala; Devaki nurses them with her milk, and, released from the curse, they bow and ascend to the gods' abode.
characters: Krishna; Balarama; Devaki; the six sons
themes: restoration; mother's love; release from curse

working_title: Krishna Visits Shrutadeva and Bahulashva
one_line_summary: Krishna, to please both the sage Shrutadeva and King Bahulashva of Mithila, visits both their homes simultaneously, unseen by each other.

working_title: The Brahmana's Dying Sons || In Dwaraka, a brahmana's newborn sons die one after another; he lays their bodies at the palace gate and laments the king's failure to protect his subjects.
one_line_summary: In Dwaraka, a brahmana's newborn sons die one after another; he lays their bodies at the palace gate and laments the king's failure to protect his subjects.

working_title: Arjuna's Failed Vow || Arjuna boasts that he will protect the brahmana's next child, but though he fences the delivery-room with arrows, the newborn vanishes, and the brahmana rebukes him.
one_line_summary: Arjuna boasts that he will protect the brahmana's next child, but though he fences the delivery-room with arrows, the newborn vanishes, and the brahmana rebukes him.

working_title: Krishna and Arjuna Journey to Recover the Brahmana's Sons
one_line_summary: Krishna, to save the despairing Arjuna, mounts his divine chariot and carries him beyond the darkness to Vaikuntha, where they behold the Supreme Lord upon the serpent Ananta.
variant_notes: BP: divine chariot beyond the darkness to Vaikuntha; Harivamsha: across the ocean and the seven cosmic mountains.

working_title: The Brahmana's Sons Are Restored
one_line_summary: The Supreme Lord tells Krishna and Arjuna that he himself had taken the brahmana's sons to bring them together, and returns the children, whom they restore to the brahmana.
characters: Krishna; Arjuna; the Supreme Lord; the brahmana
variant_notes: BP: the Supreme Lord returns the children; Harivamsha: three stolen boys and the new-born infant restored.

working_title: Garuda Reports the Site of Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Garuda returns from reconnoitering Kushasthali and praises it as a fitting abode; Krishna, knowing Jarasandha unslayable, resolves to leave Mathura.

working_title: The Yadavas Resolve to Abandon Mathura for Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Fearing Kalayavana's assault, the Vrishnis and Andhakas make Krishna their president and resolve to leave Mathura for Kushasthali (Dwarka).

working_title: Rukmavati's Swayamvara and Marriage || Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.
one_line_summary: Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Aniruddha nuptials (bp10c_050/vp5_028_01) and Pradyumna's marriage to Rukmavati.

working_title: Pradyumna Duels Jayanta in the Sky || Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.

working_title: Pradyumna Saves the Maidens by Illusion || When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.
one_line_summary: When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.

working_title: Pradyumna Binds the Bribed Kings with Shiva's Nooses || Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.
one_line_summary: Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.
characters: Pradyumna; Nandi; Shiva; Sisupala; Rukmi; Bhagadatta

working_title: Nikumbha Fells Arjuna and Pradyumna; Krishna Duels Him || Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.
one_line_summary: Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.

working_title: Krishna's Stratagem: the Actor Bhadra and the Swan Emissaries || Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.
one_line_summary: Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.
characters: Krishna; Indra; Bhadra (actor); Pradyumna; Prabhavati; swans

working_title: Pradyumna in Bee Form Meets Prabhavati || Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.

working_title: The Danava Princesses Arm Their Yadava Husbands || When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.
one_line_summary: When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.
characters: Prabhavati; Pradyumna; Chandravati; Gada; Gunavati; Shamba

working_title: Pradyumna Fights with Ananta as Charioteer || Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
one_line_summary: Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
characters: Pradyumna; Ananta; Indra; Gada; Shamba; Jayanta; Pravara

working_title: Pradyumna Duels Vajranabha || Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.
one_line_summary: Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.

working_title: Pradyumna Slays Vajranabha with Krishna's Discus || Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.
one_line_summary: Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.
characters: Pradyumna; Vajranabha; Krishna; Gada; Shamba; Sunabha

working_title: Indra and Krishna Install the Four Young Kings || Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.
one_line_summary: Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.

working_title: The Yogamaya Appears Before Krishna and Rama || The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.
one_line_summary: The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.

working_title: Mayavati Reveals the Truth to Pradyumna || When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.
one_line_summary: When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.

working_title: Pradyumna Fells Shamvara's Standard to Provoke Him || To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.
one_line_summary: To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.

working_title: Pradyumna Slays the Hundred Sons of Shamvara || In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.
one_line_summary: In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.

working_title: Pradyumna Slays Shamvara's Four Ministers || Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.
one_line_summary: Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.

working_title: Shamvara's Illusions and Pradyumna's Counters || Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.
one_line_summary: Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.

working_title: Narada Reveals Pradyumna's True Identity and Arms Him || Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.
one_line_summary: Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.

working_title: Narada's Riddle: Who Is Truly Great || When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.
one_line_summary: When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.

working_title: Garuda Quenches Bana's Protective Fire || As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.
one_line_summary: As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.

working_title: Krishna Strikes Down Angira and the Fire-Gods || Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.
one_line_summary: Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.

working_title: Chitralekha Comes to Dwarka as Usha's Emissary || Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.
one_line_summary: Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.

working_title: Aniruddha Routs Vana's Soldiers || When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.
one_line_summary: When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.

working_title: The Goddess Durga Releases Aniruddha from His Bonds || Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.
one_line_summary: Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.

working_title: Krishna, Balarama and Pradyumna Fly to Sonitpura on Garuda
one_line_summary: To rescue Aniruddha from Bana, Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna fly out on Garuda, Krishna assuming eight arms and innumerable heads with his weapons.
themes: divine form; march to war; rescue

working_title: The Yadavas' Grief and Search for Aniruddha || Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.
one_line_summary: Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.
characters: Krishna; Aniruddha's wives; Ahuka; Viprithu; Anadhrishti

working_title: Narada Reveals Aniruddha's Captivity by Vana || Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.
one_line_summary: Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.

working_title: Kartikeya Duels the Yadavas; Krishna Counters Brahmashira || Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.
one_line_summary: Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.

working_title: Krishna Celebrates Aniruddha's Wedding and Grants the Kingdom to Kumbhanda || Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.
one_line_summary: Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.

working_title: Usha Is Welcomed into the Yadu Family || Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.
one_line_summary: Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.
characters: Ahuka; Usha; Aniruddha; Devaki; Rukmini; Revati

working_title: Vishnu Commands Yogamaya to Transfer Balarama and Arrange the Exchange
one_line_summary: Vishnu directs Yogamaya to draw the unborn Balarama from Devaki's womb into Rohini's, and to be born herself as Nanda's daughter.

working_title: Kamsa Dashes the Infant and Yogamaya Warns Him
one_line_summary: When Kamsa dashes the girl against a stone she rises as the eight-armed goddess Yogamaya, warns him that his slayer is already born, and Kamsa, shaken, repents and frees Devaki and Vasudeva.

working_title: Shambara Steals the Infant Pradyumna
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, Kama reborn as Krishna's son, is abducted as a newborn by the asura Shambara and thrown into the sea.
variant_notes: Age at abduction varies: six days (VP), seventh night (Harivamsha); BP just 'newborn'. All cast him into the sea.

working_title: Mayavati (Rati) Rescues and Raises Pradyumna || A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.
one_line_summary: A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Shambara-stole cluster (bp10c_024); Harivamsha expands (hv_b2_042-047).

working_title: Pradyumna Slays Shambara
one_line_summary: Armed with the great science of countering illusion, Pradyumna challenges and beheads the demon Shambara.
variant_notes: BP: 'great science of countering illusion'; VP: slays the enchanter with his own eighth illusion.

working_title: Pradyumna Returns to Dvaraka and Is Recognized
one_line_summary: Pradyumna returns to Dvaraka with Mayavati; Rukmini recognizes her long-lost son, and the city rejoices.
variant_notes: Harivamsha has Rukmini recognize him by a dream and Vrishni marks; BP has her recognize her long-lost son.

working_title: Aniruddha Is Betrothed to Rukmi's Granddaughter
one_line_summary: Setting aside his grudge for his sister Rukmini's sake, Rukmi weds his granddaughter Rocana to Aniruddha in Bhojakata.
variant_notes: Both: Aniruddha wed to Rukmi's granddaughter, celebrated at Bhojakata.

working_title: Bana's Thousand Arms and Shiva's Boon || The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.
one_line_summary: The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.
variant_notes: BP-only background beat for the Bana episode.

working_title: Usha Dreams of Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Bana's daughter Usha dreams of a beloved youth, and her friend Chitralekha paints the princes to identify him as Aniruddha.
variant_notes: Both: Usha dreams of the youth and Chitralekha paints the princes until she recognizes Aniruddha.

working_title: Aniruddha Is Brought to Usha and They Unite
one_line_summary: Chitralekha, by her mystic power, carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura, where he lives secretly with Usha.
variant_notes: BP: Chitralekha carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura; Harivamsha: they are united in secret Gandharva marriage.

working_title: Bana Captures and Binds Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Bana's guards discover the secret union; Bana finds Aniruddha with Usha and binds him with serpent-nooses.
variant_notes: BP and VP: bound with serpent-nooses; Harivamsha: fettered with serpentine shafts via Tamasika illusion.

working_title: Krishna and Shiva Duel with Divine Weapons
one_line_summary: The Vrishnis besiege Shonitapura; Shiva and Skanda fight for Bana, and Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons.
variant_notes: BP: Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons; Harivamsha: exchange of Indra/Shiva/Varuna/Vaishnava weapons.

working_title: Krishna Stupefies Shiva and Puts Skanda to Flight
one_line_summary: Krishna throws the Jrimbhana astra, stupefying Shiva, and Pradyumna routs Skanda, while Bana's mother shields her son.
variant_notes: BP: Jrimbhana astra; VP: weapon of yawning. VP bundles the three-headed Fever's defeat here.

working_title: Krishna Severs Bana's Thousand Arms and Spares Him
one_line_summary: Krishna severs Bana's thousand arms with his discus; Shiva intercedes, and Krishna spares Bana with four arms remaining.
variant_notes: Arms remaining varies: four (BP) vs two (Harivamsha/VP). Shiva intercedes in all.

working_title: Aniruddha and Usha Are Freed
one_line_summary: Bana surrenders, gives Aniruddha and Usha to Krishna, and the Vrishnis return in triumph to Dvaraka.
variant_notes: BP: Bana surrenders and hands them over; Harivamsha: the serpent-bonds fall away at the sight of Garuda.

working_title: Pradyumna's Valor and Wounding || Pradyumna destroys Shalva's illusions and slays many foes, but is struck senseless by Dyuman's mace; recovering, he rebukes his charioteer for drawing him from the field.
one_line_summary: Pradyumna destroys Shalva's illusions and slays many foes, but is struck senseless by Dyuman's mace; recovering, he rebukes his charioteer for drawing him from the field.

working_title: Krishna's Sons and the Yadu Lineage
one_line_summary: The text enumerates Krishna's sixteen thousand wives and his many sons — Pradyumna, Aniruddha and others — and traces the line through Vajra, the sole Yadu survivor of the coming internecine war.

working_title: Balarama Marries Revati
one_line_summary: Some days after the founding of Dwaraka, Baladeva weds Revati, the daughter of king Revata, with Rishabha's consent.
variant_notes: Harivamsha: weds Revati, daughter of king Revata; VP: after sporting two months in Vraja, marries Revati daughter of Raivata.

working_title: Krishna Defeats the Besieging Kings and Demons || Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed the hosts of Kala, Magadha (Jarasandha) and Shalva that besieged Dwaraka, and slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed the hosts of Kala, Magadha (Jarasandha) and Shalva that besieged Dwaraka, and slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.
characters: Krishna; Jarasandha; Shalva; Bana; Mura; Dantavakra
themes: defence of the city; demon-slaying; valour
variant_notes: Recall bundling many battles (Kala, Magadha, Shalva, Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra).

working_title: Balarama Revisits Vraja
one_line_summary: Balarama returns to Nanda's Gokula, consoles the pining gopis with Krishna's message, and stays two months in their company.

working_title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Intoxicated by Varuni, Balarama summons the Yamuna to sport; when she refuses, he drags her with his plough until she begs forgiveness.

working_title: The Gorilla Dvivida Ravages the Land || The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.
one_line_summary: The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Dvivida-slaying cluster (bp10c_069/vp5_036_01).

working_title: Balarama Slays the Ape Dvivida
one_line_summary: The ape Dvivida insults Balarama and his women; Balarama fells him with his mace, freeing the land of the menace.
variant_notes: BP: Balarama fells him with his mace; VP: a single blow of the fist.

working_title: Balarama Seeks Samba's Release and Is Insulted || Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.
one_line_summary: Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Balarama-drags-Hastinapura cluster (bp10c_072).

working_title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura with His Plough
one_line_summary: Enraged, Balarama seizes his plough and drags the city of Hastinapura toward the Ganga; the terrified Kauravas surrender Samba and Lakshmana.
variant_notes: All: Balarama hooks his plough under the city and threatens to fling it into the Ganga; the Kauravas yield Samba and the bride.

working_title: Balarama Slays the Suta Romaharshana || At Naimisha, Balarama, seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.
one_line_summary: At Naimisha, Balarama, seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.

working_title: The Sages Prescribe Balarama's Penance || The sages instruct Balarama that to expiate the brahmana-slaying he must slay the demon Balvala, who defiles their sacrifice, and then perform a year-long pilgrimage.
one_line_summary: The sages instruct Balarama that to expiate the brahmana-slaying he must slay the demon Balvala, who defiles their sacrifice, and then perform a year-long pilgrimage.

working_title: Balarama Slays the Demon Balvala || When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down with his plough and crushes his head with his mace, and the sages shower Balarama with honors.
one_line_summary: When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down with his plough and crushes his head with his mace, and the sages shower Balarama with honors.

working_title: Indra Asks Krishna to Befriend Arjuna
one_line_summary: Indra asks Krishna to protect his son Arjuna, Krishna's cousin, in the coming war of the Bharatas.

working_title: Krishna Rejoices as Arjuna Wins Draupadi
one_line_summary: Seeing Arjuna string the stiff bow and shoot the mark, Krishna is filled with joy and approaches the disguised Pandava with a white robe and a garland of flowers.

working_title: Krishna Names the Pandavas to Balarama
one_line_summary: At Draupadi's svayamvara, Krishna, seated among the Yadava chiefs, recognizes the five Pandavas disguised as Brahmins and tells Balarama who each of them is.
characters: Krishna; Balarama; Yudhishthira; Bhima; Arjuna; Nakula; Sahadeva; Draupadi

working_title: Krishna Stops the Angry Kings from Attacking the Pandavas
one_line_summary: When the insulted kings rush to attack Drupada and the Pandavas, Krishna declares that Draupadi has been justly won and persuades the monarchs to abandon the fight.
characters: Krishna; Bhima; Arjuna; Drupada; Karna; Salya

working_title: Krishna and Balarama Meet the Pandavas at the Potter's House
one_line_summary: Suspecting the Pandavas to be alive, Krishna and Balarama come to the potter's house, touch Yudhishthira's and Kunti's feet, and warn the disguised brothers to keep hidden.

working_title: Krishna Sends Wedding Gifts to the Pandavas After Draupadi's Marriage
one_line_summary: After the Pandavas' marriage to Draupadi, Krishna sends them gold ornaments, costly robes, gems, elephants, horses, and crores of gold coins, which Yudhishthira accepts with joy.
variant_notes: Duplicate events from the same Ganguli translation (1.201).

working_title: Krishna Counsels the Pandavas to Return to Their Kingdom
one_line_summary: At Vidura's visit, Krishna (Vasudeva) advises that the Pandavas should accept their ancestral kingdom, and Drupada defers to his judgment.

working_title: Krishna Settles the Pandavas in Indraprastha and Returns to Dwaravati
one_line_summary: After the Pandavas receive half the kingdom, Krishna helps them establish Indraprastha, then takes his leave and returns to Dwaravati with Balarama.

working_title: Krishna Embraces Arjuna at Prabhasa and Hosts Him at Dwaraka
one_line_summary: During Arjuna's forest exile, Krishna learns of his arrival at Prabhasa and goes to meet him; the two friends, Nara and Narayana of old, embrace and Krishna hosts Arjuna at Dwaraka for many days.

working_title: Krishna Counsels Arjuna to Abduct Subhadra
one_line_summary: At the Raivataka festival, Krishna notices Arjuna's love for his sister Subhadra and advises him to carry her away by force, the celebrated Kshatriya form of marriage.
variant_notes: Krishna's counsel precedes the abduction; cf. bp10d_045/mb_a1_009.

working_title: Krishna Comes to Indraprastha Bearing Nuptial Gifts
one_line_summary: Hearing that Arjuna has reached Indraprastha with Subhadra, Krishna arrives with the Yadava host and presents the Pandavas with cars, cows, mares, mules, and damsels as nuptial gifts.
variant_notes: Nuptial gifts for Subhadra's marriage (distinct from Draupadi's wedding gifts); cf. bp10d_045.

working_title: Krishna Performs the Birth Rites of Abhimanyu
one_line_summary: Krishna stays on at Indraprastha with Arjuna, and when Subhadra bears Abhimanyu, Krishna performs the infant's birth rites; the child grows dear to him.

working_title: Krishna and Arjuna Sport on the Yamuna and Receive a Mysterious Brahmana
one_line_summary: In summer Krishna and Arjuna go with friends to sport on the banks of the Yamuna, where a radiant Brahmana suddenly approaches the seated heroes.
variant_notes: First beat of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_013 (Agni reveals himself), bp10c_038 (Bhagavata summary).

working_title: Agni, in Brahman Disguise, Seeks Krishna and Arjuna's Help to Burn Khandava
one_line_summary: The Brahmana reveals himself as Agni and asks Krishna and Arjuna to shield him from Indra's rains so he can consume the Khandava forest.
locations: Khandava forest; the banks of the Yamuna
variant_notes: Second beat of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_012, bp10c_038.

working_title: Krishna Vows the Earth Shall Drink the Blood of the Pandavas' Foes
one_line_summary: Visiting the exiled Pandavas in the forest, an enraged Krishna vows that the earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karna, Dussasana and Sakuni, and that Yudhishthira will be reinstalled on the throne.
variant_notes: Forest-visit vow; parallel to pre-war vow in mb_b_001/mb_b_002.

working_title: Arjuna Pacifies the Wrathful Krishna
one_line_summary: When Krishna, inflamed by the Pandavas' wrongs, seems bent on consuming all creatures, Arjuna recites his former divine feats to calm him, and Krishna answers that he and Arjuna are Nara and Narayana.

working_title: Krishna Promises Draupadi She Will Be Queen Again
one_line_summary: To the weeping Draupadi, Krishna vows that the wives of her enemies shall weep over their slain husbands and that she will once more be queen of kings, his words never futile.
variant_notes: Forest-visit promise; parallel to pre-war vow mb_b_002.

working_title: Krishna Laments His Absence from the Dice Game
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that had he been present at Dwarka he would have prevented the dice game by counsel or force, and that his absence while fighting Salwa caused the Pandavas' calamity.

working_title: Krishna Appears in Answer to Draupadi's Prayer
one_line_summary: When Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples and Draupadi has no food to offer, she prays to Krishna, who instantly leaves Rukmini's bed and comes to her.
variant_notes: cf. mb_e_005, mb_e_006 (Akshaya-patra episode).

working_title: Krishna Eats a Single Grain and Satisfies Durvasa and His Disciples
one_line_summary: Krishna finds one grain of rice sticking to Draupadi's vessel, eats it, and by that act the sage Durvasa and his ten thousand disciples feel their stomachs full and flee.
variant_notes: cf. mb_e_004.

working_title: Krishna Reassures the Pandavas and Departs
one_line_summary: After the frightened Munis flee, Krishna appears to the anxious Pandavas, assures them that Durvasa is gone and that the virtuous never suffer, then returns home.
variant_notes: cf. mb_e_005.

working_title: Krishna Sends Akrura to Hastinapura
one_line_summary: Krishna visits Akrura's home and dispatches him to Hastinapura to learn whether the Pandavas are treated justly.

working_title: Kunti Confides Her Sorrow to Akrura
one_line_summary: In Hastinapura, Kunti tearfully tells Akrura of the Pandavas' persecution and prays to Krishna for protection.

working_title: Akrura Counsels Dhritarashtra
one_line_summary: Akrura advises Dhritarashtra to treat the Pandavas as his own sons, then returns and reports to Krishna and Balarama.

working_title: Krishna Visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha
one_line_summary: Krishna visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha, is joyously received by Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Draupadi and Kunti, and stays four months.
variant_notes: Earlier visit (10.58); distinct from the Rajasuya arrival bp10d_006.

working_title: Krishna Grants the Khadava Forest to Agni
one_line_summary: Krishna, as Arjuna's charioteer, helps him give the Khadava forest to Agni, who bestows the Gandiva bow and inexhaustible quivers.
variant_notes: Condensed Bhagavata account of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_012 (Brahmana arrives), mb_a1_013 (Agni seeks help).

working_title: Krishna Arrives at Indraprastha for the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: Krishna arrives at Indraprastha, where Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins and Kunti embrace him with overflowing love.
characters: Krishna; Yudhishthira; Bhima; Arjuna; Kunti; Draupadi
variant_notes: Bhagavata (10.71) frames the arrival as an emotional reunion/embrace; Mahabharata (2.32) frames it as arriving with treasure.

working_title: Krishna Pacifies the Yadavas After Arjuna's Abduction of Subhadra
one_line_summary: Arjuna, disguised as a renunciant, wins Krishna's sister Subhadra and carries her off; when Balarama grows angry, Krishna pacifies him and he sends wedding gifts.
variant_notes: Bhagavata (10.86) condenses abduction + pacification; Mahabharata (1.223) details the defense of the alliance.

working_title: Krishna Washes the Feet of the Brahmanas
one_line_summary: At the Rajasuya, Krishna the lord of all worlds humbly takes up the menial office of washing the feet of the Brahmanas.
variant_notes: Krishna's menial service at the sacrifice; precedes the first-honor episode; cf. bp10d_015/mb_a2_012.

working_title: Shishupala Incites the Kings to Battle
one_line_summary: Shishupala rallies the angry monarchs to obstruct the sacrifice, and Krishna perceives that the assembled kings are preparing for a rush.
variant_notes: Follows Shishupala's outburst; cf. bp10d_016/mb_a2_013.

working_title: Bhishma Foretells That Krishna Will Destroy Shishupala
one_line_summary: As Yudhishthira fears for his sacrifice, Bhishma declares the kings mere barking dogs before the sleeping lion of the Vrishnis, and that Vishnu has resolved to take back Shishupala's energy.
variant_notes: Bhishma's foretelling within the Shishupala episode; cf. bp10d_016.

working_title: Krishna Grants Shishupala's Mother the Boon of a Hundred Offences
one_line_summary: When the frightened queen begs a boon, Krishna promises to pardon a hundred offences of Shishupala for her sake, a promise that now nears its limit.
variant_notes: The hundred-offences boon, now expiring; cf. bp10d_017.

working_title: Narada Announces the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: Narada arrives at the assembly and announces that Yudhishthira will perform the Rajasuya sacrifice, requesting Krishna's consent and presence.
variant_notes: Narada's announcement precedes the request; cf. bp10d_007/mb_a2_010.

working_title: Yudhishthira Requests the Rajasuya and Krishna Approves
one_line_summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna's permission and blessing to perform the Rajasuya, and Krishna approves, promising to win the kings of the earth for him.
variant_notes: Same permission moment; Bhagavata 10.72 vs Mahabharata 2.32.

working_title: The Pandavas Conquer the Directions
one_line_summary: Yudhishthira sends his four brothers to conquer the four quarters, and they return laden with tribute for the sacrifice.
variant_notes: Follows the Rajasuya permission; cf. bp10d_007.

working_title: Krishna Receives the First Honor (Arghya) at the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: Sahadeva declares Krishna alone worthy of the highest honor at the sacrifice, and Yudhishthira washes Krishna's feet and worships him before all.
variant_notes: Bhagavata credits Sahadeva's declaration; Mahabharata credits Bhishma's direction.

working_title: Shishupala's Outburst Against Krishna
one_line_summary: Enraged at Krishna's honor, Shishupala rises and heaps insults on Krishna, calling him a cowherd unworthy of worship; the assembly rebukes him and some draw weapons.
characters: Shishupala; Krishna; the assembly; the Pandavas

working_title: Krishna Slays Shishupala
one_line_summary: Krishna, restraining his own men, cuts off Shishupala's head with the sharp-edged discus, and Shishupala's effulgence merges into Krishna.

working_title: The Rajasuya Completed
one_line_summary: Krishna completes the Rajasuya for Yudhishthira, gives the priests their fees, stays some months, and departs; only Duryodhana cannot bear the Pandavas' splendor.
variant_notes: Rajasuya conclusion; cf. bp10d_015.

working_title: Duryodhana's Humiliation in Maya's Hall
one_line_summary: In the illusory assembly hall built by Maya, Duryodhana mistakes water for floor and falls; Bhima and the women laugh, and Duryodhana departs burning with shame and hatred.
variant_notes: Duryodhana's humiliation follows the sacrifice; cf. bp10d_018.

working_title: Shalva Wins the Flying City Saubha || Shalva, friend of the slain Shishupala, vows to destroy the Yadavas and wins from Shiva through austere penance the flying iron city Saubha, built by Maya.
one_line_summary: Shalva, friend of the slain Shishupala, vows to destroy the Yadavas and wins from Shiva through austere penance the flying iron city Saubha, built by Maya.

working_title: Shalva Besieges Dwaraka || Shalva arrives at Dwaraka in the indestructible flying city Saubha and rains weapons, rocks and serpents upon the city, terrifying its people.
one_line_summary: Shalva arrives at Dwaraka in the indestructible flying city Saubha and rains weapons, rocks and serpents upon the city, terrifying its people.

working_title: Krishna Returns to the Battle || Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka, orders his chariot against Shalva, and joins the fight, shattering Shalva's weapons.
one_line_summary: Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka, orders his chariot against Shalva, and joins the fight, shattering Shalva's weapons.

working_title: Shalva's Illusion of Vasudeva's Death
one_line_summary: Shalva conjures the illusion that his men have captured and beheaded Vasudeva before Krishna's eyes; Krishna, briefly appearing grief-stricken, then sees through the sorcery.
variant_notes: BP: Krishna briefly appears grief-stricken then sees through the sorcery; MB: Krishna swoons and drops the Sharnga bow.

working_title: Krishna Destroys the Flying City Saubha and Slays Shalva
one_line_summary: Krishna cuts off Shalva's arm, shatters the flying city Saubha with his mace, and beheads Shalva with the discus as he attacks on foot.
variant_notes: MB splits it: discus cuts Saubha in twain (mb_a2_027), then cleaves Salwa (mb_a2_028); BP bundles both (mace shatters Saubha, discus beheads Shalva).

working_title: Krishna Slays Dantavakra and Viduratha || Dantavakra attacks Krishna with a mace to avenge Shishupala and Shalva; Krishna crushes his chest, then beheads his brother Viduratha with the discus.
one_line_summary: Dantavakra attacks Krishna with a mace to avenge Shishupala and Shalva; Krishna crushes his chest, then beheads his brother Viduratha with the discus.

working_title: Draupadi Invokes Krishna as She Is Dragged and Disrobed
one_line_summary: As Dussasana drags her before the assembly and strips her, Draupadi cries out to Govinda, Kesava and Janarddana to rescue her from the Kaurava ocean.
variant_notes: Invocation beat; cf. mb_a2_020.

working_title: Krishna Protects Draupadi with Endless Robes
one_line_summary: Moved by Draupadi's call, Krishna comes to her aid from compassion; the unseen Dharma covers her so that as each garment is dragged off another appears, hundreds of robes protecting her honour.
variant_notes: Protection beat; cf. mb_a2_019.

working_title: Draupadi Appeals to Krishna for Vengeance
one_line_summary: Draupadi, clutching her dishevelled hair, reminds Krishna of her humiliation in the assembly and begs him to avenge her on the Kauravas.
variant_notes: Pre-war appeal; parallel to forest-visit vow mb_a2_021.

working_title: Krishna Vows the Kuru Women Will Weep
one_line_summary: Krishna comforts the weeping Draupadi and swears that the women of the Kuru race will soon weep as she does, with their kinsmen slain.
variant_notes: Pre-war vow; parallel to forest-visit promise mb_a2_023.

working_title: The Pandavas Charge Krishna with the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Before his departure for Hastinapura, Bhima, Arjuna and Nakula each address Krishna, urging him to seek peace with the Kauravas and entrusting their cause to him.

working_title: Krishna Accepts the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Asked by Arjuna to go as envoy, Krishna agrees to go to Dhritarashtra to seek peace for the good of both the Pandavas and the Kurus.

working_title: Krishna Prepares His Chariot and Sets Out for Hastinapura
one_line_summary: After his morning rites, Krishna has his car armed with his conch, discus and mace; Garuda alights on its flagstaff, and he mounts and sets out with Satyaki.

working_title: Yudhishthira Entrusts Krishna with Messages for Kunti and the Elders
one_line_summary: Yudhishthira, following Krishna some distance, asks him to salute and comfort his grieving mother Kunti and to greet Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Vidura and all the elders.

working_title: Arjuna's Parting Warning and Bhima's Roar
one_line_summary: Arjuna warns that if Duryodhana acts improperly he will annihilate the Kshatriyas, and Bhima, hearing this, sets forth a terrible shout that makes all bowmen tremble.

working_title: Krishna Meets the Celestial Rishis Led by Parashurama
one_line_summary: On the road Krishna alights to worship a band of celestial Rishis; Jamadagni's son Parashurama embraces him and says they come to witness the conclave and hear his words.

working_title: Krishna's Auspicious Journey to Hastinapura
one_line_summary: As Krishna journeys to Hastinapura, dread omens fall on the Kuru capital while wherever he passes the road becomes auspicious with showers of flowers; he passes the night at Vrikasthala.

working_title: Duryodhana's Lavish Pavilions That Krishna Ignores
one_line_summary: Duryodhana builds gem-studded pavilions to receive Krishna, but Krishna arrives at the Kuru capital without casting a single glance at them.

working_title: Vidura Exposes the Plan to Bribe Krishna
one_line_summary: When Dhritarashtra plans lavish gifts to win Krishna over, Vidura declares the gifts betray deception and that Krishna can never be separated from Arjuna.

working_title: Duryodhana Resolves to Imprison Krishna; Bhishma Departs in Anger
one_line_summary: Duryodhana announces his plan to imprison Krishna; Dhritarashtra is pained and Bhishma, denouncing the wicked scheme, rises in rage and leaves.

working_title: Krishna Enters Hastinapura and Meets Dhritarashtra
one_line_summary: Welcomed by Bhishma, Drona and the Dhartarashtras, Krishna enters Hastinapura, where the blind king Dhritarashtra and all the elders rise to honour him.

working_title: Krishna Comforts the Grieving Kunti
one_line_summary: Krishna visits his aunt Kunti, who pours out her sorrows for her exiled sons; he consoles her and assures her she will soon see the Pandavas victorious.

working_title: Krishna Refuses Duryodhana's Hospitality
one_line_summary: Duryodhana invites Krishna to eat at his house, but Krishna refuses, saying envoys eat only after their mission succeeds and that he will accept food from Vidura alone.

working_title: Vidura Warns Krishna of Duryodhana's Wickedness
one_line_summary: That night Vidura tells Krishna his coming was ill-judged, describing Duryodhana's vices and his belief that he can never be persuaded to make peace.

working_title: Krishna's Resolve: The Merit of Striving for Peace
one_line_summary: Krishna answers Vidura that he came knowing Duryodhana's wickedness, for great is the merit of one who strives to save the earth from destruction even if he fails.

working_title: Krishna Enters the Kuru Assembly
one_line_summary: Krishna rides in procession to the Kuru court, enters arm-in-arm with Vidura and Satyaki, and after the Rishis are seated takes his seat in the assembly.

working_title: Krishna's Plea for Peace Before the Assembly
one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, Krishna urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and restore the Pandavas' share of the kingdom, to save the world from slaughter.

working_title: Parashurama Reveals Krishna and Arjuna as Nara and Narayana
one_line_summary: Parashurama, in the assembly, tells the tale of Dambhodbhava and declares that Nara and Narayana of old are now Arjuna and Krishna, urging Duryodhana to make peace.

working_title: Krishna's Appeal to Duryodhana
one_line_summary: At Dhritarashtra's request, Krishna approaches Duryodhana directly and urges him, with reasoned counsel, to make peace with the Pandavas for the good of his own race.

working_title: Duryodhana's Refusal: Not a Needle-Point of Land
one_line_summary: Duryodhana rejects Krishna's counsel, claiming he has done no wrong, and vows that not even land covered by the point of a needle will be given to the Pandavas while he lives.

working_title: Krishna's Rebuke of Duryodhana's Crimes
one_line_summary: With eyes red in anger, Krishna recounts Duryodhana's crimes — the dice plot, Draupadi's humiliation, the attempts to burn and poison the Pandavas — and foretells his downfall.

working_title: Krishna Urges the Elders to Bind Duryodhana
one_line_summary: After Duryodhana storms out, Krishna tells the elders that they are guilty for not seizing the wicked king, citing how he himself slew Kansa to save his kinsmen.

working_title: The Plot to Seize Krishna; Satyaki's Alarm
one_line_summary: Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana resolve to seize Krishna by force; Satyaki, reading the signs, alerts Krishna and arrays the troops.
characters: Krishna; Satyaki; Duryodhana; Karna; Sakuni; Dussasana; Kritavarman

working_title: Krishna Defies the Conspirators
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Dhritarashtra that if they wish to seize him by violence they may try, for he could make over all of them to the Pandavas, but he will not commit a censurable deed.

working_title: Krishna Reveals His Universal Form
one_line_summary: Laughing at Duryodhana's boast to seize him, Krishna bursts into his universal form — gods issuing from his body, the whole court dazzled, all but a few closing their eyes in terror.
characters: Krishna; Duryodhana; Bhishma; Drona; Vidura; Sanjaya

working_title: Krishna Departs as Dhritarashtra Pleads Powerlessness
one_line_summary: With the assembly witnessed, Krishna takes leave of the elders, declares he will return to Yudhishthira, and mounts his car to depart as Dhritarashtra protests his powerlessness.

working_title: Krishna Relays Kunti's Message: The Duty of a Kshatriya
one_line_summary: Krishna reports the failed embassy to Kunti and carries back her charge to Yudhishthira to recover his kingdom by the prowess of his arms as a Kshatriya should.

working_title: Kunti's Exhortation: The Story of Vidula and Sanjaya
one_line_summary: Kunti instructs Krishna to carry the ancient tale of Vidula, who shamed her defeated son Sanjaya back into battle, as an exhortation to war for Yudhishthira.

working_title: Kunti's Final Messages and Krishna's Leave-Taking
one_line_summary: Kunti gives Krishna parting words for Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi and the twins, recalling the celestial voice that promised Arjuna victory, and Krishna takes his leave of her.

working_title: Krishna Takes Karna Upon His Chariot and Returns to Upaplavya
one_line_summary: Krishna dismisses the Kuru chiefs, takes Karna upon his chariot, deliberates with him at length, then dismisses him and returns swiftly to Upaplavya.
variant_notes: cf. mb_e_008 (Karna's leave-taking).

working_title: Krishna Reveals Karna's Birth and Offers Him the Kingdom
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Karna he is Kunti's firstborn son and therefore a Pandava, and offers to have him installed as king of the whole earth with the Pandavas as his followers.

working_title: Karna Refuses, Pledging Loyalty to Duryodhana
one_line_summary: Acknowledging he is Kunti's son by Surya, Karna refuses the kingdom, declaring that Adhiratha and Radha who raised him are his parents and that he will not betray Duryodhana.
characters: Krishna; Karna; Duryodhana; Adhiratha; Radha; Kunti

working_title: Karna's Prophecy of the Coming War as a Sacrifice
one_line_summary: Karna foretells the war as a great sacrifice of arms with Krishna as its witness, describing how each hero will play a priestly part, and asks Krishna to keep their talk secret.

working_title: Karna Worships Krishna and Takes His Leave
one_line_summary: On the road from Hastinapura, Karna worships Krishna and recounts omens and visions foretelling the Kauravas' defeat; Krishna replies that the destruction of the earth is at hand, and the two part.
variant_notes: cf. mb_b_031.

working_title: Krishna Returns to Upaplavya and Reports the Failure of the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Krishna returns from Hastinapura and reports to the Pandavas that Duryodhana rejected his true and beneficial words in the assembly.

working_title: Krishna Guides Arjuna Against Ashvatthama's Brahmastra
one_line_summary: After Ashvatthama releases the Brahmashira weapon at the Pandavas, a terrified Arjuna calls on Krishna, who tells him only a brahmastra can counter it; Arjuna discharges it and, at Krishna's word, withdraws both blazing weapons to save the worlds.

working_title: Krishna's Verdict on Ashvatthama
one_line_summary: When Ashvatthama, the murderer of the sleeping children, is dragged before Krishna and the Pandavas, Krishna urges that the brahmin-slayer must be punished but not slain, and pronounces the compromise Arjuna carries out: strip his jewel and shave his head, sparing his life.

working_title: Bhishma's Passing in Krishna's Presence
one_line_summary: Lying on his bed of arrows at the auspicious northern solstice, Bhishma fixes his gaze on Krishna standing before him, glorifies him as Narayana himself, and passes away with his mind merged in the Lord, while the sages and Pandavas look on.

working_title: The Kurukshetra War
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how the earth shook at Kurukshetra as the armies of the warring cousins gathered, and how Duryodhana lay at the last with his thigh broken, the burden of the earth lifted by Krishna's design.
characters: Krishna; Duryodhana; the Pandavas; the Kauravas
themes: war; the fall of Duryodhana; the lifting of the earth's burden

working_title: Krishna Names Dhrishtadyumna Commander of the Pandava Army
one_line_summary: When Yudhishthira asks who should lead the seven Akshauhinis, Krishna approves the candidates and names Dhrishtadyumna as the commander-in-chief.

working_title: Krishna Declares That War Is Now Inevitable
one_line_summary: Pressed by Yudhishthira for guidance, Krishna answers that Duryodhana bears no good will and that, since the Pandavas will not abandon their property, war must now take place.

working_title: Krishna Is Chosen as Arjuna's Charioteer
one_line_summary: As the Pandavas marshal their army for Kurukshetra, Krishna is chosen as Arjuna's guide and the driver of his steeds.

working_title: Balarama Refuses to Take Sides and Departs on Pilgrimage
one_line_summary: Balarama, unwilling to fight against either the Pandavas or Duryodhana, declares he follows Krishna's cause but departs to the Saraswati tirthas rather than watch the Kauravas' destruction.

working_title: Krishna Directs Arjuna to Hymn Durga
one_line_summary: On the eve of the battle Krishna tells Arjuna to recite his hymn to Durga; the goddess appears in the sky, grants victory, and both warriors blow their conches.

working_title: Krishna Places the Chariot Between the Armies
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's request Krishna drives the chariot between the two assembled armies so Arjuna can survey the kinsmen he must fight.

working_title: Arjuna's Despair and Collapse
one_line_summary: Seeing his kinsmen arrayed on both sides, Arjuna is overcome with pity, his bow Gandiva slips from his hand, and he casts aside his weapons and sinks down on his chariot.

working_title: Arjuna Surrenders to Krishna as Disciple
one_line_summary: Unable to see his duty, Arjuna lays down his arms in spirit and begs Krishna to instruct him as his disciple.

working_title: Krishna Grants Celestial Sight and Reveals the Vishvarupa
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna gives him divine sight and reveals his supreme universal form filling the heavens.

working_title: Krishna Declares 'I Am Death'
one_line_summary: Within the cosmic form Arjuna sees the warriors rushing into Krishna's flaming mouths, and Krishna reveals himself as all-consuming Time commanding Arjuna to be his instrument.

working_title: Krishna Returns to His Gentle Form
one_line_summary: Terrified and repentant, Arjuna begs Krishna to resume his familiar form; Krishna comforts him and restores him to his senses.

working_title: Arjuna Resolves to Fight
one_line_summary: His delusion dispelled, Arjuna declares he will do Krishna's bidding and returns to battle.

working_title: Krishna's Overture to Karna
one_line_summary: After the Gita, Krishna approaches Karna and invites him to fight for the Pandavas until Bhishma falls, but Karna refuses out of loyalty to Duryodhana.
variant_notes: cf. mb_b_032 (pre-war offer to Karna).

working_title: Krishna Consoles Yudhishthira After the First Day's Battle
one_line_summary: Distraught at Bhishma's slaughter of his army, Yudhishthira speaks of retiring to the woods; Krishna consoles him and points to Sikhandin as Bhishma's destined slayer.

working_title: Krishna Drives Arjuna's Chariot Against Bhishma
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's bidding, Krishna drives the chariot straight toward Bhishma; in the ensuing duel Bhishma strikes Krishna himself between the breasts with three arrows.

working_title: Arjuna Restrains Krishna, Who Relents and Returns to the Chariot
one_line_summary: Arjuna seizes the enraged Krishna and stops him at the tenth step, vowing not to withdraw from the fight; Krishna is gratified, returns to the chariot, and sounds the Panchajanya.

working_title: Krishna Counsels Arjuna to Let Karna Pass
one_line_summary: Krishna holds Arjuna back from fighting Karna, warning that Karna still holds the infallible dart that Vasava (Indra) gave him.

working_title: Krishna Lends His Car to Satyaki
one_line_summary: Krishna foresees Satyaki's need, summons his charioteer Daruka by blowing his conch, and lends his own celestial car to Satyaki for the fight with Karna.

working_title: Krishna Embraces and Praises Arjuna After the Vow
one_line_summary: When Arjuna's vow against Jayadratha is fulfilled, Krishna embraces him, and Arjuna credits the victory entirely to Krishna's grace.

working_title: Krishna Shows Arjuna the Slain Battlefield
one_line_summary: As they ride back across the field, Krishna points out to Arjuna the fallen kings, elephants, and horses slain by his shafts.

working_title: Krishna Rallies the Broken Pandava Host
one_line_summary: Seeing the Panchalas routed by Drona and Karna, Krishna urges Arjuna to cast away fear and advance against the two great warriors.

working_title: Krishna Sends Ghatotkacha Against Karna
one_line_summary: Krishna keeps Arjuna from Karna and instead commands the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha to fight Karna at night, so that Karna's infallible dart is spent on him.

working_title: Krishna Directs Ghatotkacha to Slay Alayudha
one_line_summary: When Bhima is hard-pressed by the Rakshasa Alayudha, Krishna tells Ghatotkacha to abandon Karna for the moment and first slay Alayudha.

working_title: Krishna Rejoices at Ghatotkacha's Fall
one_line_summary: While the Pandavas mourn Ghatotkacha, Krishna dances and shouts for joy, then reveals the cause: Karna's infallible dart is now spent and Karna is mortal.

working_title: Krishna Recounts His Slaying of Enemy Kings
one_line_summary: Krishna explains to Arjuna that, for the Pandavas' good, he contrived the deaths of Jarasandha, Ekalavya, Sisupala and Ghatotkacha himself.
characters: Krishna; Arjuna; Jarasandha; Ekalavya; Sisupala; Ghatotkacha
themes: divine plan; protection of dharma; past deeds

working_title: Krishna Explains His Protection of Arjuna
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Satyaki how he always shielded Arjuna from Karna's dart, stupefying Karna so the weapon was never hurled at Partha.

working_title: Krishna Consoles the Grieving Yudhishthira
one_line_summary: When Yudhishthira is overwhelmed by grief at Ghatotkacha's death, Krishna urges him to rise and fight rather than sink into despondency.

working_title: Krishna Devises the Ashvatthama Stratagem
one_line_summary: Seeing Drona unbeatable in battle, Krishna counsels the Pandavas to abandon fair means and tell Drona that his son Ashvatthama is slain, so he will lay down his arms.

working_title: Krishna Urges Yudhishthira to Speak the Untruth
one_line_summary: As Drona is about to annihilate the Pandava army, Krishna presses the truth-loving Yudhishthira to tell the half-truth that Ashvatthama is dead.
themes: falsehood for a just end; moral dilemma; necessity

working_title: Krishna Points Out Karna's Rampage and Urges Arjuna
one_line_summary: Krishna, as Arjuna's charioteer, shows Arjuna how Yudhishthira is being pursued and how Karna is ravaging the Pandava army, urging him to advance and slay Karna.

working_title: Krishna Advises Arjuna to See the Wounded King First
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Arjuna that Yudhishthira has been deeply wounded by Karna and advises him to first see and comfort the king before slaying Karna.

working_title: Krishna Drives Arjuna to Yudhishthira's Side
one_line_summary: Krishna drives the chariot at great speed to the wounded Yudhishthira, and the two Krishnas alight and worship the king's feet.

working_title: Krishna Offers Sudarsana to Slay Karna
one_line_summary: Seeing Karna baffle Arjuna's weapons, Krishna rebukes Arjuna's slackness and offers him the razor-edged Sudarsana discus to strike off Karna's head.

working_title: Krishna Sinks the Chariot to Save Arjuna
one_line_summary: When Karna looses the snake-arrow Aswasena at Arjuna's head, Krishna presses the chariot down into the earth with his feet so that the arrow only sweeps off Arjuna's diadem.

working_title: Krishna Identifies the Snake Aswasena
one_line_summary: Krishna names the attacking snake as Aswasena, whose mother Arjuna slew at Khandava, bids Arjuna slay it, and after Arjuna cuts it down raises the sunken chariot with his arms.

working_title: Krishna Urges Arjuna to Slay the Distressed Karna
one_line_summary: When Arjuna hesitates to strike the stupefied Karna, Krishna urges him not to spare a fallen foe; Karna's chariot-wheel then sinks into the earth and he appeals to Arjuna's righteousness for a moment's respite.
themes: duty; ruthlessness in war; dharma; vulnerability

working_title: Balarama Tries to Halt the Mace-Duel
one_line_summary: Hearing that Bhima and Duryodhana are locked in their final mace-duel, Balarama goes to stop the slaughter but, unable to part the two, returns to Dwaraka.

working_title: Kunti's Farewell Hymn to Krishna
one_line_summary: As Krishna prepares to leave Hastinapura for Dwaraka, Queen Kunti offers a parting eulogy recalling how he saved her family from poison, fire, exile and weapons, and asks only that his remembrance ever bind her; Krishna smiles and grants her prayer.

working_title: Krishna Departs Hastinapura for Dwaraka
one_line_summary: After restoring Yudhishthira to the throne and staying some months to comfort his relatives, Krishna takes leave of the grieving Pandavas and women of Hastinapura and sets out for Dwaraka, journeying through many kingdoms.

working_title: Krishna's Homecoming to Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Krishna reaches his own prosperous realm of Anarta, sounds his conch, and is welcomed by the joyful citizens, his father Vasudeva, Balarama, Ugrasena and his queens, who receive him with offerings and embrace.
characters: Krishna; Vasudeva; Balarama; Ugrasena; Devaki; the citizens of Dwaraka

working_title: Vyasa Consoles Arjuna and Parikshit Is Enthroned
one_line_summary: Vyasa tells Arjuna that Krishna's departure was the will of time and recounts Ashtavakra's curse on the Apsarasas; Arjuna installs Vajra in Mathura, and the Pandavas place Parikshit on the throne.
variant_notes: cf. vp5_038_01 (Dwaraka sinks).

working_title: The Pilgrimage to Samanta-panchaka
one_line_summary: On the occasion of a solar eclipse, the Yadavas journey to Samanta-panchaka to bathe and give gifts, and there a vast reunion of kings and kinsfolk takes place.

working_title: Reunion with Nanda and Yashoda
one_line_summary: Nanda and the cowherds arrive, and Krishna, Balarama, Yashoda, Devaki and Rohini embrace one another, recalling the old days in Gokula.
characters: Krishna; Balarama; Nanda; Yashoda; Vasudeva; Devaki; Rohini

working_title: Krishna's Counsel to the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna meets the gopis, who have long pined for him, embraces them, and teaches them that all beings abide in him, and that their love for him grants immortality.

working_title: Nanda's Farewell
one_line_summary: Vasudeva, overcome with love, laments that riches blinded him to old friends, and Nanda, honored by the Yadavas with rich gifts, departs for Mathura with the cowherds.

working_title: Krishna Sports with His Sixteen Thousand Wives
one_line_summary: Krishna sports in the lakes with his sixteen thousand wives, splashing and being splashed, while the women's songs of longing express their single-hearted devotion.

working_title: Krishna Substitutes an Iron Statue for Bhima
one_line_summary: Sensing Dhritarashtra's murderous intent, Krishna drags away the real Bhima and substitutes an iron statue, which the blind king crushes in his embrace; Krishna then reveals the trick and consoles him.

working_title: Krishna Counsels Dhritarashtra to Govern His Wrath
one_line_summary: Krishna admonishes Dhritarashtra that his sorrow is his own fault and urges him to restrain his wrath; the king is pacified and embraces and blesses the Pandavas.

working_title: Gandhari Curses Krishna; He Accepts with a Smile
one_line_summary: Grieving her sons, Gandhari curses Krishna that in the thirty-sixth year he will see his own kinsmen slain and himself perish in the wilderness; Krishna, smiling, accepts that only the Vrishnis themselves can destroy the Vrishnis.
variant_notes: Gandhari's curse; cf. mb_d_013 (the sages' curse).

working_title: Krishna Rebukes Gandhari
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Gandhari to arise and not grieve, declaring the carnage came through her own fault and Duryodhana's wickedness, not through him.

working_title: Arjuna Asks Krishna to Repeat the Gita; Krishna Offers the Anugita
one_line_summary: After the war, Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the Gita's teaching and asks Krishna to repeat it; Krishna says he cannot recite it again in detail and instead narrates an old history (the Anugita).

working_title: Krishna's Final Instruction to Uddhava
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how, as the Yadavas destroyed themselves, Krishna sat at the foot of an ashvattha tree and, finding Uddhava there, granted him the ancient teaching and the supreme state, commanding him to go to Badari.
locations: the bank of the Sarasvati; at the foot of an ashvattha tree
themes: the final teaching; the supreme state; grace
variant_notes: The final teaching; cf. Uddhava's departure cluster (bpc1_024).

working_title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Krishna charges Uddhava with a message to console Nanda, Yashoda and the pining gopis.

working_title: Uddhava Arrives in Vrindavan and Nanda Longs for Krishna
one_line_summary: Uddhava reaches Vrindavan at dusk, is honored by Nanda, who asks after Krishna and remembers his deeds.

working_title: Uddhava Begs Krishna Not to Leave Him Behind
one_line_summary: Seeing the fearful omens in Dwaraka and Krishna's intention to depart, Uddhava falls at his feet and pleads that he cannot bear to be separated even for a moment and begs to be taken along; Krishna, granting his wish, begins to instruct him.

working_title: Yadu Meets the Wandering Avadhuta
one_line_summary: King Yadu meets a serene, fearless brahmin avadhuta and, astonished at his freedom, asks how he attained such wisdom; the avadhuta answers that he has twenty-four gurus from whom he drew his understanding.
characters: Krishna; Uddhava; King Yadu; the avadhuta brahmin

working_title: The Avadhuta's Lessons from the Elements
one_line_summary: The avadhuta relates what he learned from the earth, wind, sky, water, fire, moon and sun: forbearance, detachment, unaffectedness, purity, untaintedness, waxing and waning, and the one soul reflected in many bodies.

working_title: The Pigeon and the Hunter's Net
one_line_summary: A pigeon so bound to his mate and chicks that when a hunter's net traps his family he casts himself into the same net and perishes with them, teaching Krishna's hearers that clinging to home and family destroys.
characters: the pigeon; the pigeon's mate; the chicks; the hunter
themes: attachment; grief; the snare of home; cautionary tale

working_title: The Python's Contentment and the Ocean's Depth
one_line_summary: The avadhuta learns from the python to accept whatever food chance brings without striving, and from the ocean to remain deep, full and unmoved whether rivers pour in or not.
characters: the avadhuta; the python; the ocean

working_title: The Moth and the Bee
one_line_summary: From the moth, which perishes in the flame, the avadhuta learns that desire for a woman's beauty destroys; from the bee he learns to take only the essence from many flowers without storing anything up.
characters: the avadhuta; the moth; the bee

working_title: The Elephant, the Honey-Gatherer, the Deer and the Fish
one_line_summary: The avadhuta learns from the elephant, ensnared by lust for the decoy she-elephant, from the honey-gatherer, whose hoard others enjoy, from the deer, snared while listening to music, and from the fish, hooked through the tongue, how the senses lead one to ruin.
characters: the avadhuta; the elephant; the honey-gatherer; the deer; the fish

working_title: Pingala the Courtesan's Renunciation
one_line_summary: The courtesan Pingala, waiting through the night for a client who never comes, is seized with disgust at her own longing, renounces it, and sleeps in peace, teaching that hope is the worst of pains and despair the highest joy.

working_title: The Osprey, the Child, the Maiden and the Arrow-Maker
one_line_summary: The avadhuta learns from the osprey (letting go of prey seized by stronger birds), the child (freedom from care), the maiden (solitude — she broke her bangles one by one to stop their clinking), and the arrow-maker (one-pointed concentration).
characters: the avadhuta; the osprey; the child; the maiden; the arrow-maker

working_title: The Serpent, the Spider and the Wasp
one_line_summary: The avadhuta learns from the serpent (dwelling in another's abandoned hole, homeless), from the spider (who spins the web from himself and withdraws it again), and from the wasp (who becomes what it meditates upon).
characters: the avadhuta; the serpent; the spider; the wasp

working_title: The Swan Teaches the Kumaras
one_line_summary: Asked by his disciples about the swan form, Krishna recounts how Brahma's sons Sanaka and the others, unable to get an answer from Brahma, were taught by Krishna himself appearing as a swan (hamsa), who resolved their doubt.
characters: Krishna (as the swan); the Sanaka Kumaras; Brahma; Uddhava

working_title: The Miserly Brahmin of Avanti
one_line_summary: A wealthy but miserly brahmin of Avanti, spurned by his own relatives and stripped of his wealth, is seized with dispassion, becomes a wandering mendicant, and, enduring the mockery and blows of the crowd, sings the song of the mendicant: the mind alone is the cause of joy and sorrow.

working_title: Pururava's Lament for Urvashi
one_line_summary: King Pururava (Aila), mad with grief when the nymph Urvashi leaves him, pursues her naked and weeping; realizing his delusion, he sings the song of Aila on the futility of attachment to women, and attains peace.

working_title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama
one_line_summary: Krishna commands Uddhava to leave for his hermitage at Badarikashrama and abide in the teaching he has received; the grief-stricken Uddhava circumambulates him, places his feet upon his own head, and departs bearing Krishna's sandals.
themes: farewell; the final teaching; separation; devotion

working_title: Narada Prophesies the Ocean Will Swallow Dwarka || Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.
one_line_summary: Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.

working_title: The Sages Curse Samba and the Yadavas
one_line_summary: Yadu boys dress Samba as a pregnant woman and ask the visiting sages what 'she' will bear; the angered sages curse that he will bring forth an iron mace to destroy the clan, and the mace appears, is ground and cast into the sea, and its remaining iron, swallowed by a fish, later becomes the hunter's arrow.
characters: Krishna; Samba; the Yadu boys; the sages; Ugrasena
themes: curse; fate; arrogance; the iron mace

working_title: Krishna Foresees the Yadavas' Self-Destruction || Uddhava recalls Krishna's deliberation that the Yadu warriors, themselves the remaining burden of the earth, could be destroyed in no other way than by their own quarrel, and that when he acted, they would destroy themselves.
one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls Krishna's deliberation that the Yadu warriors, themselves the remaining burden of the earth, could be destroyed in no other way than by their own quarrel, and that when he acted, they would destroy themselves.
themes: fate; divine design; the removal of the burden
variant_notes: Recall; cross-ref the Yadavas' self-destruction (vp5_037_03).

working_title: Sesha Departs from Balarama
one_line_summary: As Krishna watches, the great serpent Sesha issues from Balarama's mouth and enters the ocean, hymned by saints and serpents, and Ocean comes forth to receive him.

working_title: The Yadavas Journey to Prabhasa
one_line_summary: Seeing the terrible omens rising in Dwaraka, Krishna tells the Yadava elders to leave at once for the holy tirtha of Prabhasa, and they cross the sea in boats and chariots to worship there.
variant_notes: Command (Bhagavata 11.30, Mahabharata 16.2) and execution (Bhagavata 3.3) of the same journey.

working_title: The Yadava Fratricide at Prabhasa
one_line_summary: Drunk on maireya wine at Prabhasa, the Yadavas, deluded by Krishna's maya and the brahmins' curse, fall upon one another, and when their weapons fail they seize the eraka reeds — which have become iron clubs — and annihilate one another; Balarama then yields up his body in yoga.

working_title: Samva Brings Forth the Iron Bolt; Wine Is Prohibited
one_line_summary: The next day Samva brings forth the iron bolt; king Ugrasena has it ground to powder and cast into the sea, and at the command of Krishna, Rama and others a prohibition on wine is proclaimed throughout Dwaraka.
variant_notes: cf. mb_d_013.

working_title: Krishna Sends Daruka for Arjuna; Vabhru Is Slain
one_line_summary: Krishna sends Daruka to summon Arjuna and commands Vabhru to protect the women; Vabhru, still dazed with wine, is slain by the iron bolt that springs from a hunter's mallet.
variant_notes: cf. bpc1_028 (Daruka's errand).

working_title: Arjuna Brings News of the Yadava End
one_line_summary: Arjuna returns from Dwaraka broken and weeping and tells Yudhishthira how the Yadavas, deluded by a brahmin's curse and drunk on wine, slew one another with their fists, and how Krishna then departed the earth, after which the Kali age set in.
characters: Krishna; Arjuna; Yudhishthira; Kunti; the Yadavas
themes: destruction; separation; the Kali age; fate
variant_notes: Arjuna's report of the Yadava end; cf. bpc1_030.

working_title: Vidura Meets the Grieving Uddhava
one_line_summary: On the banks of the Yamuna, Vidura meets Uddhava, who is plunged in grief and remembrance of Krishna's departure, and hears him lament that the Yadavas never recognized the Lord who dwelt among them.

working_title: The Abhiras Rob Arjuna
one_line_summary: Leading Krishna's widowed wives and wealth from Dwaraka, Arjuna is set upon by Abhira robbers; his bow Gandiva goes slack, his weapons fail, and the thieves carry off the women and treasure.
variant_notes: Aftermath of the submergence; cf. bpc1_030.

working_title: Brahma and the Gods Urge Krishna to Return to His Abode
one_line_summary: After one hundred and twenty-five years, Brahma and the assembled gods come to Dwaraka, praise Krishna, and remind him that the earth's burden is lifted and his clan is nearly consumed by the curse, asking him to return to his own abode.
variant_notes: Prefigures the departure; cf. bpc1_029.

working_title: The Hunter Jara Shoots Krishna's Foot
one_line_summary: After the Yadavas' destruction, Krishna sits in meditation at the foot of a pippala tree; the hunter Jara, mistaking Krishna's foot for a deer's, shoots it with the arrow made from the mace's iron, then, seeing the four-armed Lord, falls at his feet in terror.
locations: a forest near Prabhasa; at the foot of a pippala tree
themes: fate; the hunter's arrow; divine play; forgiveness
variant_notes: Vishnu Purana (5.37) condenses the shooting with the forgiveness and departure.

working_title: Krishna's Last Message to Daruka
one_line_summary: Krishna consoles the hunter, granting him heaven, and when his charioteer Daruka weeps at his feet, sends him to Dwaraka with the final message: the Yadavas are destroyed, Balarama is gone, and the sea will swallow Dwaraka, so let the people follow Arjuna to Indraprastha.
themes: the final message; compassion; the coming flood
variant_notes: cf. mb_d_019; follows the shooting (bpc1_027).

working_title: Krishna's Final Departure / Ascension
one_line_summary: As Brahma, Shiva and the hosts of gods watch, Krishna, seeing Brahma before him, closes his lotus eyes, draws his opulences into himself, consumes his body with the fire of yoga, and enters his own abode, his path unfathomable even to the gods.
themes: departure; yogic fire; the return to the abode; divine mystery
variant_notes: Mahabharata's account also includes comforting the hunter Jara.

working_title: The Sea Swallows Dwaraka
one_line_summary: After Krishna's departure, his queens and family ascend the funeral pyres, Arjuna performs the last rites, and the sea floods and swallows Dwaraka — all but the Lord's own dwelling; Arjuna leads the survivors to Indraprastha and installs Vajra.
themes: grief; the flood; the end of an era; succession
variant_notes: Includes the queens' pyres and Arjuna's last rites; Bhagavata adds installing Vajra.

working_title: Krishna Entrusts the Women to Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Krishna returns to Dwaraka, tells his father Vasudeva to protect the women until Arjuna comes, touches his father's feet, and retraces his steps to comfort the wailing ladies.

working_title: Vrikasura's Lethal Boon from Shiva
one_line_summary: The asura Vrikasura wins from Shiva the boon that whoever's head he touches will die, then tries to test it on Shiva himself, who flees in terror to Vaikuntha.
variant_notes: cf. bp10d_048 (Vishnu's rescue of Shiva).

working_title: Vishnu Saves Shiva from Vrikasura
one_line_summary: Vishnu, appearing as a young brahmachari, tricks Vrikasura into touching his own head, and the asura destroys himself, freeing Shiva.

working_title: Bhrigu Tests the Three Gods
one_line_summary: Sent by the sages to test who is greatest, Bhrigu finds Brahma and Shiva angered, but Vishnu, far from being offended, apologizes and serves him, proving Vishnu supreme.
